summary: Howe and Klevdal reinterpret basic local Shimura varieties and their non-minuscule analogues as moduli of neutral admissible pairs (families of B_dR^+-latticed isocrystals whose modified bundles are semistable of slope 0), for any connected linear algebraic group G. On the way they extend to non-reductive G the basic strata of Bun_G (Theorem 4.2.2), the B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian and its Schubert cells (Theorem 5.0.4, Proposition 5.2.1), the admissible loci (Propositions 7.3.3–7.3.4) and basic duality (Theorem 8.5.1). They relate lattices and filtrations over diamonds (Theorems 3.2.1, 3.3.1), build period domains of p-adic Hodge structures, and show that Hodge and Hodge–Tate loci of tensors and the resulting special subdiamonds are closed, including for non-reductive subgroups (Propositions 6.4.1, 7.5.2). The main theorem is a bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem (Theorem 9.1.3, Theorem A in the minuscule case). For the two analytic structures on a basic infinite-level space given by the Hodge and Hodge–Tate towers, the Zariski closure in one structure of an irreducible analytic set of the other is a special subvariety, so the closed bi-analytic sets are exactly the special subvarieties. Theorem B is the sideways version for any neutral admissible pair over a rigid variety. The proof uses the Tannakian formalism, a Baire-category argument for Hodge-generic classical points (Lemma 9.3.1), Part I's openness of Galois images and a constant-rank computation. The atlas plans the reductive foundations (Bun_G, Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians, local shtuka moduli, relative Fargues–Fontaine curves, period sheaves). It has none of the theory of admissible pairs, Part I included, so this is routed to one new roadmap. Five general inputs go to their owners as sources: seminormal full faithfulness to D6, Scholze's functor M to P8, B(G, μ) to BG1, the Rapoport–Viehmann and Gleason–Lourenço inputs to HS2, and Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev to LD.6. Two small Part IIs take general facts on algebraic groups and on rigid-analytic Zariski geometry. Fourteen source issues are recorded: twelve misprints, one gap (the proof of Theorem 7.2.3 for singular bases), and v1's incorrect Lemma 4.1.1, already corrected in v2. After the review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26) there are 191 items (2 library, 22 planned, 167 missing) and 48 source issues. E1–E14 are confirmed. The new findings are local gaps, each with a verified repair. Smoothness hypotheses are used for singular S (Lemmas 6.3.3 and 7.4.4, Theorem 7.2.3). Theorem 3.3.1(3) lacks a descent step. Connectedness of motivic Galois groups is never proved. Lemma 9.3.1 is applied to Z that is only irreducible, and Part I Corollary 5.5.3 is used over non-strict fields. There are also two errors in §7.5: Lemma 7.5.1 needs Y connected, and the proof of Proposition 7.5.2 fails when H^1(Q_p, H) → H^1(Q_p, G) has a kernel. Lemma 9.3.3's 'if' direction is false beyond points. Theorems A, B and 9.1.3 stand.

items.name: Admissible pairs and basic admissible pairs over C (Part I)
items.statement: Let C/Q_p be an algebraically closed non-archimedean extension and B_dR^+ = B_dR^+(C). (1) A B_dR^+-latticed isocrystal is a pair (W, L) with W an isocrystal over Q̆_p and L ⊆ W ⊗_{Q̆_p} B_dR a B_dR^+-lattice; a morphism (W, L) → (W', L') is a morphism of isocrystals f with f(L) ⊆ L', strict if f(L) = f(W)_{B_dR} ∩ L'. (2) An admissible pair is a B_dR^+-latticed isocrystal (W, L_ét) such that the modification E(W)_{L_ét} at ∞ of the vector bundle E(W) on the Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_{C♭} is semistable of slope zero. (3) It is basic if the slope decomposition W = ⊕_λ W_λ induces L = ⊕_λ L_λ with L_λ = (W_λ ⊗ B_dR) ∩ L. AdmPair(C) ⊇ AdmPair^basic(C) are the resulting categories.
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Definition 5.1.1; recalled in Section 1.3, p. 10 (not p. 9), and used in Definition 7.1.1, p. 39 (arXiv v2)

items.name: p-adic Hodge structures over C (Part I)
items.statement: A B_dR^+-latticed Q_p-vector space (V, L) (V finite-dimensional over Q_p, L ⊆ V ⊗_{Q_p} B_dR a B_dR^+-lattice) is a p-adic Hodge structure of weight λ ∈ Q if the modification (V ⊗_{Q_p} O_FF)_L at ∞_C is semistable of slope −λ/2. The category HS(C) of p-adic Hodge structures is the full subcategory of Q-graded B_dR^+-latticed Q_p-vector spaces whose degree-λ part has weight λ.
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Definition 4.2.1; recalled in Section 1.3, p. 10, and used in Definition 6.0.1, p. 35 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review note: Statement checked against the Part I TeX: the slope −λ/2 is Part I Definition 4.2.1. Part I's proof of Lemma 4.3.2 writes 'semistable of slope λ/2', a sign slip in Part I that does not affect the argument, which is symmetric in the sign. The item correctly follows the definition. items.name: HS(C) and AdmPair(C) are connected neutral Tannakian; basic admissible pairs are p-adic Hodge structures (Part I)
items.statement: (1) HS(C) is abelian and is a connected neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω_ét: (V, L) ↦ V. (2) AdmPair(C) is a connected neutral Tannakian category with fibre functor ω_ét = H^0(FF_{C♭}, E(W)_{L_ét}); it is equivalent to the isogeny category of rigidified Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules; and (ω_ét, ω_{L_dR}), with ω_{L_dR} the de Rham lattice c_dR^{-1}(W ⊗ B_dR^+), is an equivalence of Tannakian categories ω_HS: AdmPair^basic(C) ≅ HS(C), the weight grading coming from the slope decomposition.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Lemma 4.3.2, Theorem 4.3.5 and Theorem 5.1.6; used in Section 6, p. 36, Lemma 6.2.1, p. 36, Proposition 6.2.3, p. 37, Theorem 7.1.2, p. 40, and Section 8.3, p. 51

items.name: Motivic Galois groups and the canonical reduction of structure group (Part I)
items.statement: Let T be a neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω, let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group, and let 𝒢: Rep G → T be an exact tensor functor with ω∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std. Put H = Aut^⊗(ω|_⟨𝒢⟩). This is MT(𝒢) when T = HS(C) and MG(𝒢) when T = AdmPair(C). Then H is a linear algebraic group, a trivialization ω∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std identifies H with a closed subgroup of G, and 𝒢 has a canonical refinement to an H-structure, i.e. a factorization Rep G → Rep H → T (Part I §2.1.3). For T = HS(C), H is the subgroup of G preserving every Hodge–Tate line ℓ ∈ HT^{2k}(𝒢(V)) for V ∈ Rep G and k ∈ Z (Part I Theorem 4.5.1). For T = AdmPair(C), H is the subgroup preserving every Hodge line ℓ ∈ Hdg^{2k}(𝒢(V)) (Part I Theorem 5.3.1). For a general T, the same Chevalley argument shows that H is the stabilizer of the lines underlying rank-one subobjects of the 𝒢(V).
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2): Sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.3; Theorem 4.5.1 (Section 4.5); Theorem 5.3.1 (Section 5.3); definitions of MT(𝒢) in Section 4.4 and of MG(𝒢) in Section 5.2. Used in Section 6.1, p. 36, Section 6.3, p. 37, Section 7.2, p. 41, and Lemma 7.5.1, p. 46 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item states the line-stabilizer characterization for an arbitrary neutral Tannakian T. Part I proves it only in two cases: for p-adic Hodge structures (Theorem 4.5.1, using weight-2k Hodge–Tate lines HT^{2k}) and for admissible pairs (Theorem 5.3.1, using Hodge lines Hdg^{2k}). The locator omits both theorems. The general statement is true by Chevalley's argument, since an H-stable line in 𝒢(V) is a subobject in ⟨𝒢⟩ ≅ Rep H, but Part I does not state it. The admissible-pair case, which Section 7.4 uses through the Hodge locus, is not mentioned in the item.

items.name: Filtrations, lattices and bilatticed G-bundles over a point; goodness and type (Part I)
items.statement: Let L be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 and B^+ a complete discretely valued L-algebra with algebraically closed residue field C, fraction field B and uniformizer t. In the p-adic case L = C̄_0 and B^+ = B_dR^+(C); in the complex case B^+ = C[[t]]. Let K ⊆ L and let G be a connected linear algebraic group over K. A filtration (resp. lattice) on a G-bundle ω: Rep G → Vect(M), with M = K or C (resp. M = K), is an exact tensor functor to filtered M-vector spaces (resp. B^+-latticed K-vector spaces) together with an identification of its underlying functor with ω. For G over L, a bilatticed G-bundle is an exact L-linear tensor functor ω_bl: Rep G → Vect^bl(B), where objects are B-vector spaces with two B^+-lattices L_1, L_2. Its isomorphism class is a double coset in G(B^+)\G(B)/G(B^+). It is good of type [μ] if this double coset is G(B^+)μ(t)G(B^+). These double cosets exhaust G(B) when G is reductive, but not in general. BB_1 (resp. BB_2) sends (V, L_1, L_2) to L_1 ⊗ C (resp. L_2 ⊗ C) with the trace filtration, the image of (F^•B·L_2) ∩ L_1 (resp. (F^•B·L_1) ∩ L_2).
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Definition 3.1.1, Definition 3.1.5 (Section 3.1), Section 3.2 and Definition 3.2.5; used in Section 3, p. 19 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Two problems. (a) The base field is wrong. In Part I §3, B^+ is a complete discretely valued algebra over an algebraically closed field L of characteristic 0, with residue field C (in the p-adic case L = C̄_0, the algebraic closure in C of C_0 = W(κ_C)[1/p]). Definition 3.1.5 takes K a subfield of L, not an arbitrary K ⊆ C, and bilatticed G-bundles are L-linear functors for G over L. (b) Goodness and type are defined in Part I Definition 3.2.5, which the locator omits.

items.name: Goodness of a bilatticed G-bundle is exactness of either trace filtration (Part I)
items.statement: For a bilatticed G-bundle ω_bl the following are equivalent: (1) ω_bl is good; (2) BB_1∘ω_bl is a filtered G-bundle (i.e. is exact); (3) BB_2∘ω_bl is a filtered G-bundle. In this case, if ω_bl has type [μ], then BB_1∘ω_bl has type [μ^{-1}] and BB_2∘ω_bl has type [μ].
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Theorem 3.2.6; used in the introduction to Section 3, pp. 19–20, and in the proof of Theorem 3.2.1, p. 23 (not p. 22) (arXiv v2)

items.name: Types can only go up under representations when a lattice is not good (Part I)
items.statement: Let G be a connected linear algebraic group over C with Levi decomposition G = M ⋉ U, g = mu ∈ G(C((t))), and [μ] the conjugacy class of cocharacters of M with m ∈ M(C[[t]]) t^μ M(C[[t]]). For any representation ρ: G → GL_n, if [ν] indexes the Schubert cell containing ρ(g), then [ν] ≥ [ρ∘μ] in the Bruhat order. If ρ is faithful, then [ν] = [ρ∘μ] if and only if g ∈ G(C[[t]]) t^μ G(C[[t]]).
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Theorem 3.5.1; used in Section 5 (p. 32) and in the proof of Proposition 5.2.1, p. 34 (arXiv v2), after identifying B_dR^+(C) ≅ C[[t]] (Part I Example 3.0.1)
items.note: Review note: Part I states the order as the dominance order on multisets of integers for GL_n. The item's 'Bruhat order' is the same order.

items.name: When the filtration determines the lattice (Part I)
items.statement: (1) If the weights of [μ] in the adjoint action on Lie G are ≤ 1, then BB: Gr_[μ](C) → Fl_[μ^{-1}](C) is a bijection (for G reductive this means [μ] is minuscule). (2) If a group 𝔊 acts on B^+ preserving its maximal ideal, K = C^𝔊 ⊆ L, 𝔊 acts on K·t through an infinite-order character, and G and [μ] are defined over K, then Fl_[μ^{-1}](K) is the set of 𝔊-invariants of Gr_[μ](C); this applies to K a p-adic field, C = K̄^, 𝔊 = Gal(K̄/K) (Part I Example 3.1.10).
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Proposition 3.1.7 and Example 3.1.10; used in Section 5.3, p. 34, and the proof of Theorem 5.0.4(5), p. 35

items.name: The Kottwitz set B(G, [μ^{-1}]) and basic classes for non-reductive G
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group with unipotent radical U and [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p}. The projection G → G/U identifies B(G) = B(G/U) and the conjugacy classes of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} and (G/U)_{Q̄_p}; B(G, [μ^{-1}]) is defined as B(G/U, [μ^{-1}]) through these identifications. A class is basic if its slope morphism is central in G. For G reductive B(G, [μ^{-1}]) has a unique basic class; in general, if M ⊆ G is a Levi subgroup, B(M, [μ^{-1}]) = B(G, [μ^{-1}]), but the basic class of M may fail to be central in G, and then B(G, [μ^{-1}]) has no basic class.
items.locator: Section 1.1, pp. 3–4, and footnote 1, p. 5 (arXiv v2); Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Sections 2.2.3 and 4.4

items.name: The isocrystal of a good G-p-adic Hodge structure is the basic class (Part I)
items.statement: For a good G-p-adic Hodge structure 𝒢 over C whose weight morphism is central (for example if G = MT(𝒢)), the isocrystal class [b]_𝒢 of the associated G-admissible pair is the unique basic element of B(G, [μ^{-1}]_𝒢).
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Theorem 4.4.4; used in the proof of Proposition 6.2.3, p. 37

items.name: Existence of G-admissible pairs with given invariants (Part I)
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group, C/Q_p algebraically closed with residue field κ, C_0 = W(κ)[1/p], and C̄_0 its algebraic closure in C. A C̄_0-analytic G-admissible pair is good, with invariants [μ] and b such that b ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) (Part I Theorems 5.4.4 and 5.2.4). Conversely, for every b ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) there is a C̄_0-analytic G-admissible pair with invariants b and [μ]. To see this, choose a Levi decomposition G = MU and push out from M, which reduces to G reductive; that case is Rapoport–Viehmann, Proposition 3.1.
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Example 5.4.6 (combining Theorems 5.2.4 and 5.4.4); used in the proof of Lemma 6.2.1, p. 37, and in Proposition 7.3.3, p. 43 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The hypothesis 'A Q̄_p-analytic (more generally C̄_0-analytic)' is not Part I's. Part I Example 5.4.6 assumes a C̄_0-analytic G-admissible pair (Definition 5.4.1), where C_0 = W(κ_C)[1/p] and C̄_0 is its algebraic closure in C. A 'Q̄_p-analytic' admissible pair is not defined: the Hodge filtration lives on W ⊗_{Q̆_p} C̄_0, and Q̄_p does not contain Q̆_p. Part I's smaller class is the Q̄̆_p-analytic pairs.

items.name: Admissible pairs with good reduction give crystalline Galois representations (Part I)
items.statement: Let K be a strict p-adic field and C = K̄^. The étale realization promotes to ω_{G_K}: AdmPair^goodred(K) → Rep_{Q_p}(G_K), which is fully faithful, has essential image stable under subobjects and consisting of crystalline representations.
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Theorem 5.5.1; used in the proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42

items.name: The Galois image of an admissible pair with good reduction is open in its motivic Galois group (Part I)
items.statement: If 𝒢 is a G-admissible pair with good reduction over a strict p-adic field K and ρ: G_K → G(Q_p) is its Galois representation (after trivializing ω_ét∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std), then ρ(G_K) is an open subgroup of MG(𝒢)(Q_p). (ρ is Hodge–Tate, and by Serre's theorem on Hodge–Tate representations its image is open in its Zariski closure, which is MG(𝒢).)
items.locator: Part I (Howe–Klevdal, arXiv:2308.11065v2, whose numbering Part II's cross-references use), Corollary 5.5.3; used in the proof of Theorem 9.1.3, p. 57

items.name: Transcendence characterization of special points (Part I, Corollary C)
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group, [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p}, and b ∈ G(Q̆_p) basic. Let C/Q_p be algebraically closed with residue field κ, C_0 = W(κ)[1/p], and C̄_0 the algebraic closure of C_0 in C. Call x ∈ M_{b,[μ]}(C) special if the Tannakian structure group (motivic Galois group) of the associated G-admissible pair is a torus. If π_{L_dR}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ^{-1}](C̄_0) and π_{L_ét}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ](C̄_0), then x is special. Conversely, if x is special, then π_{L_dR}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ^{-1}](Q̄_p) and π_{L_ét}(x) ∈ Gr_[μ](Q̄̆_p).
items.locator: Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2), Corollary C (Section 1.2, 'nearly equivalent' to Part I Theorem B; proved in Part I Section 6.2); cited in Remark 1.1.6, p. 6, and in Section 1.4, p. 11 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Three problems. (a) The parenthesis misdefines C_0. In Part I, C_0 = W(κ)[1/p] for κ the residue field of C (the maximal absolutely unramified subfield), and C̄_0 is its algebraic closure in C (Part I Example 3.0.1(2)). There is no 'base field of Part I'. (b) The item uses 'special' without its Part I meaning: a point is special if the Tannakian structure group of its G-admissible pair is a torus. This is not Part II's notion of special subvariety. (c) The item does not state the standing data: G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, [μ], and b ∈ G(Q̆_p).

items.name: Tannakian reconstruction of a linear algebraic group from its representations
items.statement: For a commutative Hopf algebra H over a field k (the coordinate ring of an affine group G), the A-points G(A) are identified, naturally in the commutative k-algebra A, with the tensor automorphisms of scalar extension to A on finite-dimensional H-comodules; in particular G = Aut^⊗(ω_std) on Rep G.
items.locator: Section 7.2, p. 41; 'there is a canonical identification of G with Aut^⊗(ω_std)', p. 41; also Section 6.1, p. 36
items.note: TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GroupFunctor.lean:138 and Tannaka/Equivalence.lean:188. Review note: Library claim verified at f790474: TauCeti.Tannaka.pointsFunctorIsoTensorAutFunctor (TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Representation/Tannaka/GroupFunctor.lean:138) is the natural isomorphism, on commutative k-algebras, between the points functor of a commutative Hopf algebra H over a field k (lifted one universe) and the functor of tensor automorphisms of scalar extension on finite-dimensional comodules; fgPointTensorIsoEquiv (Tannaka/Equivalence.lean:188) is the pointwise MulEquiv. Together they give G = Aut^⊗(ω_std) as used on p. 41. Status 'library' is right.

items.name: Neutral Tannakian categories are representation categories
items.statement: Let T be a neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω. Then Aut^⊗(ω) is represented by an affine group scheme G over Q_p, and ω induces an equivalence of tensor categories T ≅ Rep G (Deligne–Milne, Theorem 2.11). G is algebraic, i.e. a linear algebraic group, if and only if T has a tensor generator (Deligne–Milne, Proposition 2.20(b)).
items.locator: Section 1.6, p. 13, not p. 12 (the reference to Deligne–Milne [14] and Part I Section 2.1); used in Sections 6.1 and 7.2, pp. 36 and 41 (arXiv v2)
items.note: MC.6 constructs tensor-automorphism groups of fibre functors of neutral Tannakian categories and proves the pro-algebraic reconstruction. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item attributes the algebraicity of Aut^⊗(ω) for a category with one tensor generator to Deligne–Milne Theorem 2.11. That result is Deligne–Milne Proposition 2.20(b). Theorem 2.11 gives the affine group scheme and the equivalence T ≅ Rep Aut^⊗(ω). Review note: MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.6 plans tensor-automorphism groups of fibre functors and 'the pro-algebraic reconstruction' for each proven neutral Tannakian category. That covers Deligne–Milne 2.11, but MC.6 names no algebraicity criterion (DM 2.20(b)). Accept planned, provided route 1 imports MC.6 for both parts. Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 1 plans the converse, G = Aut^⊗(ω_std) (item 015).

items.name: Levi decomposition of connected linear algebraic groups in characteristic zero
items.statement: A connected linear algebraic group G over a field of characteristic zero has a Levi decomposition G = M ⋉ U, U the unipotent radical and M ≅ G/U reductive, with any two Levi subgroups conjugate by U(k̄); the projection identifies conjugacy classes of cocharacters of G_{k̄} with those of M_{k̄}, and B(G) with B(M).
items.locator: Section 1.1, pp. 3–4 (unipotent radical, B(G) = B(G/U)) and footnote 1, p. 5 (Levi subgroup); used in Remark 4.1.1, p. 26, Theorem 4.2.2, p. 27, Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31, and Proposition 7.3.4, p. 43 (arXiv v2); Part I Lemma 2.1.2 (via Mostow)
items.note: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups plans the unipotent radical (Layer 5) and the Levi decomposition of parabolic subgroups (Layer 7), not Mostow's theorem for an arbitrary connected group. Review note: Missing is right; route 2 owns it. The inputs are planned: the Lie-algebra Levi decomposition in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/AdoIwasawa Layer 5 and the unipotent radical in tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups Layer 5. No stage plans Mostow's decomposition of a connected group. In characteristic 0, Levi subgroups are conjugate already by U(k), since H^1 of a unipotent group vanishes, as in Part I Lemma 2.1.2. The item's U(k̄) is weaker but correct.

items.name: The centre of a connected linear algebraic group is the kernel of the adjoint representation
items.statement: For G connected over a field of characteristic zero, Z(G) = ker(Ad: G → GL(Lie G)); hence b ∈ G(Q̆_p) is basic if and only if the isocrystal attached to b by the adjoint representation on Lie G is trivial.
items.note: Review note: Status missing confirmed: no atlas stage states Z(G) = ker Ad (searched 'kernel of the adjoint|Ker Ad|centre ... adjoint': nothing). Humphreys §13.4 (G connected, characteristic 0) is the right source, and route 2 is a reasonable owner.

items.name: Chevalley's theorem: closed subgroups are stabilizers of lines, in a countable family of representations
items.statement: Let G be a linear algebraic group over Q_p. (1) Every closed subgroup H ≤ G is the stabilizer of a line ℓ in some finite-dimensional representation of G. (2) Writing the regular representation Q_p[G] = ∪_i V_i as a countable filtered union of finite-dimensional subrepresentations, every closed subgroup is the stabilizer of a line in some exterior power ∧^j V_i (namely ∧^d(V_i ∩ I) for V_i containing generators of the ideal I of H).
items.locator: Proposition 9.3.4, p. 59, proof of (1), citing Borel, proof of Theorem 5.1; the stabilizer-of-a-line form is also used in Proposition 6.4.1, p. 39, Proposition 7.5.2, p. 47, and the proof of Theorem 9.1.3, p. 57 ('writing H as the stabilizer of a line ℓ in a representation of G')
items.note: Review note: Statement checked against p. 59 (correct in characteristic 0; the stabilizer is scheme-theoretic, which is automatic here). Route 2's brief, item (3), states exactly this. Status missing is right: no Mathlib or Tau Ceti declaration, and no atlas stage (a search for 'Chevalley' or 'stabilizer of a line' finds nothing).

items.name: Observable embeddings and quasi-affine homogeneous spaces
items.statement: (1) If G ≤ G' is an observable subgroup (the stabilizer of a vector in a representation of G'), then G'/G is quasi-affine (Thang–Bac, Theorem 9). (2) Every connected linear algebraic group G embeds as an observable subgroup of a reductive group: if ρ: G → GL_n is faithful, G is the stabilizer of a line in a representation of GL_n on which it acts through a character χ, and ρ × χ^{-1} embeds G into GL_n × G_m as an observable subgroup.
items.locator: Section 5.1, p. 33 (arXiv v2): the paragraph before Lemma 5.1.1, citing Thang–Bac, Illinois J. Math. 49 (2005), Theorem 9; announced in the discussion after Theorem 5.0.4, p. 32
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): Statement is right (it correctly has G'/G; the paper prints 'G/G′', see new issue 1). Only the page is wrong: the observable-subgroup argument and the Thang–Bac citation are on p. 33. The p. 32 mention is only the overview after Theorem 5.0.4. Review note: missing is right: ReductiveGroups Layer 3 plans only fppf quotients G/H, their representability, and Matsushima's affineness for reductive H. Observable subgroups and quasi-affine quotients are not planned anywhere, so route 2 fits.

items.name: Homogeneous spaces of reductive groups by reductive subgroups are affine
items.statement: If G ≤ G' are both reductive, G'/G is affine (Matsushima), so a faithful representation realizes Gr_G as a Zariski closed subdiamond of Gr_{GL_n} in the reductive case.
items.note: Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 3 names the affine representability of G/H for reductive H (Matsushima). Review note: Partly right. The Matsushima clause (G'/G affine for G ≤ G' both reductive) is named in tauceti ReductiveGroups Layer 3, which treats it as a theorem with hypotheses. The second clause (Gr_G is Zariski closed in Gr_{GL_n} for reductive G, SW Lemma 19.1.5) is not ReductiveGroups material: it is the affine case of item 091, and for reductive G it falls under GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:loop-geometry (v-sheaf representability). Suggest also citing GS0:loop-geometry.

items.name: Topology on rational points of algebraic varieties over p-adic fields
items.statement: Let E be a p-adic field and X a scheme of finite type over E. Affine charts give X(E) a functorial topology that is locally compact and, when X is separated, Hausdorff. For G a linear algebraic group, G(E) is a locally compact Hausdorff topological group. For a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space V, P(V)(Q_p) is a compact, totally disconnected, second-countable space. Hence every open subset of it is a countable union of compact open subsets, which is how the proof of Proposition 9.3.4(2) (p. 60) uses it.
items.locator: Proposition 9.3.4, p. 59; proof of (2), p. 60; also compact open subgroups K ≤ G(Q_p) throughout Sections 8–9
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Hausdorffness of X(E) needs X separated: for the affine line with a doubled origin, X(E) is not Hausdorff. RG2.0 itself restricts Hausdorffness to separated schemes. The paper uses only G(Q_p), compact open K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍 and P_{V_k}(Q_p), all separated. Review note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.0 plans the chart topology, its functoriality, local compactness and Hausdorffness for separated schemes, and the topological-group axioms, so 'planned' is right for those parts. It does not plan compactness of the points of projective (non-affine) schemes: it plans compactness of integral points only for affine models over O_E. It also does not plan second countability or total disconnectedness of P(V)(Q_p). RG2.0 should add these, or the item should be marked partly missing.

items.name: Diamonds, small v-sheaves, underlying spaces and locally spatial diamonds
items.statement: The v-topology on Perfd is subcanonical (ECD Definition 8.1, Theorem 8.7). A family {f_i: Y_i → X} is a v-cover if every quasi-compact open V ⊆ X is ∪_{j∈J} f_j(U_j) for some finite J and quasi-compact opens U_j ⊆ Y_j. A v-sheaf on Perf is small if it admits a surjection from a perfectoid space (ECD 12.1). A small v-sheaf is a diamond if it is X/R for X ∈ Perf and R ⊆ X × X a pro-étale equivalence relation (ECD 11.1, 11.9). Every small v-sheaf Y has a functorial underlying space |Y|, whose points are equivalence classes of maps Spa(C, C^+) → Y (ECD 12.7–12.8). For a diamond, open subdiamonds correspond to open subsets of |Y| (ECD 11.15). Spatial diamonds (qcqs, with a basis of quasi-compact opens) have spectral |Y|, and locally spatial diamonds have locally spectral |Y|. Maps of locally spatial diamonds induce locally spectral, generalizing maps (ECD 11.17–11.19). Locally spatial diamonds are closed under fibre products (ECD 11.29). A locally spatial Y has sites Y_v ⊃ Y_qpet ⊃ Y_ét ⊃ Y_fét (ECD 14.1, 11.23) and the analytic site Y_an of open subdiamonds. Every Y' → Y in Y_qpet is a locally spatial diamond (ECD 11.28).
items.locator: Section 2.1, pp. 13–14 (arXiv v2); also the Section 1 introduction, p. 3
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: (a) Maps of locally spatial diamonds induce locally spectral, not spectral, generalizing maps on |·| (ECD Proposition 11.19(iv), as the paper says). (b) The item cites ECD §14 but omits what the paper takes from it: the sites Y_v ⊃ Y_qpet ⊃ Y_ét ⊃ Y_fét and the analytic site Y_an of a locally spatial diamond, and the fact that quasi-pro-étale Y' → Y are locally spatial (ECD Corollary 11.28). The local systems of Section 2.3 are defined on these sites. Review note: Planned is right: DiamondsAndVStacks D2 covers the v-topology and subcanonicity, D4 covers diamonds, |Y|, open subfunctors and small v-sheaves (ECD §12), and D5 covers ECD 11.17–11.31. The ECD 14.1 sites are planned in DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0, which should be added to 'planned'. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): planned stages changed from DiamondsAndVStacks:D2, DiamondsAndVStacks:D4, DiamondsAndVStacks:D5 to DiamondsAndVStacks:D2, DiamondsAndVStacks:D4, DiamondsAndVStacks:D5, DiamondEtaleCohomology:C0. C0 plans the ECD §14 sites the item also uses.

items.name: Locally closed subdiamonds from locally closed generalizing subsets
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond and D ⊆ |Y| a locally closed generalizing subset. Then Z := D ×_{|Y|} Y (the subsheaf of maps f with |f| factoring through D) is a locally spatial diamond with |Z| = D (subspace topology), and f: Y' → Y factors through Z if and only if |f| factors through D.
items.locator: Section 2.1, p. 14 (the claim and its proof); stated in the Section 1 introduction, p. 3 (arXiv v2)
items.note: D5 plans ECD 11.17–11.31 (including 11.20, quasi-compact injections into locally spatial diamonds) and D1 plans ECD 7.1–7.7; the paper deduces the statement from these. Review note: The statement is planned nowhere. D5 plans ECD Proposition 11.20 and D1 plans ECD Lemma 7.3, the two inputs of the paper's short deduction, but no stage constructs D ×_{|Y|} Y or states |Z| = D. The status should be missing, owned by route 4 (as an addition to DiamondsAndVStacks D5) or route 1, with D1 and D5 as prerequisites. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): status changed from planned (DiamondsAndVStacks:D1, DiamondsAndVStacks:D5) to missing. D5 plans ECD Proposition 11.20 and D1 plans ECD Lemma 7.3, the two inputs of the paper's deduction, but no stage constructs D ×_{|Y|} Y or states |Z| = D. Routed to DiamondsAndVStacks (an addition to D5), with D1 and D5 as prerequisites.

items.name: Diamondification of analytic adic spaces
items.statement: For Y an analytic adic space over Z_p, Y ↦ Y^♢ is a functor to diamonds with |Y| = |Y^♢|, Y_ét = Y^♢_ét and Y_fét = Y^♢_fét (ECD Lemma 15.6); diamonds over Spd L are small v-sheaves on Perfd_L.

items.name: Seminormal rigid analytic varieties embed fully faithfully in diamonds
items.statement: Let L be a non-archimedean field over Q_p. Y ↦ Y^♢ factors through seminormalization and is fully faithful on seminormal rigid analytic varieties over L (Scholze–Weinstein, Berkeley Lectures, Proposition 10.2.3); for such Y, O_{Y_ét} is identified with the restriction of the v-structure sheaf O to Y^♢_ét.
items.locator: Section 2.2, p. 15; Section 1 introduction, p. 3, not p. 2 (arXiv v2)
items.note: D6 plans ECD Lemma 15.6 and says it is not full faithfulness on all analytic adic spaces; the seminormal full faithfulness is not planned.

items.name: Rigid analytic points, rigid analytic diamonds and rigid analytic subdiamonds
items.statement: Let L be a non-archimedean field over Q_p and S a diamond over Spd L. (1) A rigid analytic point of S over L is a morphism Spd L' → S over L with L'/L finite. (2) A rigid analytic diamond over Spd L is a diamond isomorphic to Y^♢/Spd L for a seminormal rigid analytic variety Y over L. (3) A rigid analytic subdiamond of S is a locally closed subdiamond that is a rigid analytic diamond over Spd L.

items.name: Classical points of rigid analytic varieties
items.statement: For Y a rigid analytic variety over L, the image in |Y| = |Y^♢| of a rigid analytic point of Y^♢ is a classical point, this gives a bijection between classical points and equivalence classes of rigid analytic points, and the classical points are dense in |Y| (on an affinoid Spa(A, A°) they are the maximal ideals of A).

items.name: Closed rigid analytic subdiamonds are Zariski closed subsets
items.statement: Let Y be a seminormal rigid analytic variety over L. Under |Y| = |Y^♢|, the closed subsets underlying closed rigid analytic subdiamonds of Y^♢ are exactly the Zariski closed subsets of |Y| (the vanishing loci of coherent ideal sheaves).
items.note: The proof uses that perfectoid spaces are uniform (a map factoring through |Z| on points factors through Z^red), properness of a quasi-compact partially proper map of rigid spaces, and BGR §9.6 Proposition 3 (proper images are Zariski closed; AdicSpacesPartII R3 plans Kiehl-type proper finiteness) and BGR 9.5.2 Corollary 7.

items.name: Zariski closed sets of rigid spaces and proper images
items.statement: In a rigid analytic variety Z, the closed sets of the Zariski topology (locally the vanishing sets of finitely many functions on each affinoid) are exactly the vanishing sets of coherent ideal sheaves (BGR 9.5.2, Corollary 7); the image of a proper map of rigid analytic varieties is Zariski closed (BGR §9.6, Proposition 3).
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 5 (the paragraph before Definition 1.1.2), and the proof of Lemma 2.2.3, p. 16 (arXiv v2)
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII R3 constructs coherent ideals and Kiehl-type proper finiteness and coherence. Review note: AdicSpacesPartII:R3 plans coherent ideals and Kiehl-type proper finiteness and coherence. Both assertions follow from these: the image of a proper f is the support of the coherent sheaf f_*O. However, R3 names neither the Zariski topology nor the proper-image theorem. Planned is acceptable only if R3 states them; otherwise route 3 should add both explicitly.

items.name: Λ-local systems on small v-sheaves
items.statement: For Λ a complete Huber ring, the constant sheaf Λ on Perf is Λ(X) = Cont(|X|, Λ), and the same formula holds for every small v-sheaf X (Mann–Werner, Corollary 3.15). A Λ-local system on X is a sheaf of Λ-modules on X_v that is v-locally isomorphic to Λ^n; Loc_Λ(X) is their full subcategory. For a Q_p-local system on a rigid analytic variety U, a Z_p-lattice exists after an étale cover (Mann–Werner, Proposition 3.10), and profinite torsors are diamonds with finite étale finite levels (ECD Lemma 10.13), so Q_p-local systems on U^♢ descend uniquely to U_ét.
items.locator: Section 2.3, p. 16, and the proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42
items.note: Review note: Missing is right. ECD Lemma 10.13 (profinite torsors are diamonds, with finite étale finite levels) is planned in DiamondsAndVStacks:D3 ('locally profinite group torsors and their representability'). The Mann–Werner results are planned in no stage.

items.name: The period sheaves B_dR^+ and B_dR on perfectoid spaces
items.statement: For an affinoid perfectoid Spa(R, R^+) over Q_p, B_dR^+(R) is the Ker θ-adic completion of W(R^{+♭})[1/[ϖ^♭]] for Fontaine's surjection θ, and B_dR(R) inverts a generator of Ker θ; these form v-sheaves B_dR^+ ⊆ B_dR on Perfd_{Q_p} with θ: B_dR^+ → O v-surjective, and over a p-adic field L they are sheaves of algebras over the constant sheaf L.

items.name: B-local systems on affinoid perfectoids are finite projective modules
items.statement: If X = Spa(A, A^+) is affinoid perfectoid over Q_p and B is one of B_dR^+, B_dR, O, then evaluation on X is an equivalence between Loc_B(X) and finite projective B(A)-modules (from the v-stack property, Scholze–Weinstein Corollary 17.1.9).
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry plans descent of finite projective modules on the completed divisor rings. Review note: Only partly planned. GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:loop-geometry plans descent of finite projective modules over the completed divisor rings, i.e. the B_dR^+ and B_dR cases (SW Corollary 17.1.9). No stage found plans the B = O case, v-descent of finite projective modules over affinoid perfectoid rings (SW Proposition 17.1.8, Kedlaya–Liu); VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1 plans descent only for bundles on the curve. Split off the O case and mark it missing, owned by route 1 or route 4.

items.name: The locus where a B_dR-point is integral is Zariski closed
items.statement: Let L be a p-adic field, S = Spa(R, R^+) affinoid perfectoid over Spa L, X an affine scheme of finite type over L and s ∈ X(B_dR(R)). The locus of S over which s lies in X(B_dR^+) is a Zariski closed, hence affinoid perfectoid, subdiamond of S.
items.note: Proof: reduce to X = A^1, where f ∈ Fil^{-i} lies in Fil^{-i+1} exactly on the vanishing set of θ(ξ^i f), and induct; Remark 2.3.3 records the transitivity of Zariski closedness used. Zariski closed subsets of affinoid perfectoids are affinoid perfectoid by Bhatt–Scholze, Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5 (PerfectoidQuotients Q4).

items.name: G(B)-local systems, G(Λ)-local systems and G(Λ)-torsors on diamonds
items.statement: (1) For G a linear algebraic group over a p-adic field L, X a locally spatial diamond over Spd L and B ∈ {O, B_dR^+, B_dR}, a G(B)-local system on X is an exact L-linear tensor functor Rep G → Loc_B(X); the trivial one is ω_std ⊗_L B. (2) For G over Q_p and Λ a complete Huber Q_p-algebra, a G(Λ)-local system is an exact tensor functor Rep G → Loc_Λ(X), and a G(Λ)-torsor is a sheaf on X_v with a right G(Λ)-action v-locally isomorphic to G(Λ).

items.name: G(Λ)-local systems are equivalent to G(Λ)-torsors
items.statement: The groupoids of G(Λ)-local systems and G(Λ)-torsors on X are equivalent, by ρ ↦ Isom(ω_std, ρ) and S ↦ (V ↦ S ×^{G(Λ)} V); a G(Q_p)-torsor is a diamond (ECD Lemma 10.13).
items.note: Review note: The statement that a G(Q_p)-torsor is a diamond (ECD Lemma 10.13) is planned in DiamondsAndVStacks:D3. The local-system/torsor equivalence itself is missing, as the item records.

items.name: O-local systems versus vector bundles
items.statement: For X a locally spatial diamond, pullback along X_v → X_ét identifies vector bundles (finite locally free O-modules on X_ét) with the O-local systems trivialized on an étale cover. If X is perfectoid every O-local system is a vector bundle; for X a rigid analytic diamond, vector bundles are those of the seminormal rigid space, O-local systems are locally free Ô-modules on the pro-étale site, and Tate twists give O-local systems that are not vector bundles.

items.name: The de Rham period sheaf OB_dR on the pro-étale site
items.statement: For S a smooth rigid analytic variety over a p-adic field L and ν: S_proét → S_ét, Scholze's period sheaf OB_dR (with the corrigendum) is a filtered ν^{-1}O_{S_ét}-algebra with an integrable connection OB_dR → OB_dR ⊗ Ω^1_S satisfying (OB_dR)^{∇=0} = B_dR compatibly with filtrations, and (OB_dR^+)^{∇=0} = B_dR^+ = Fil^0 OB_dR^{∇=0} (Scholze, Proposition 6.10).
items.locator: Section 2.5, p. 18, and Section 3.3, p. 23, not p. 24 (arXiv v2), citing Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, Proposition 6.10, with the corrigendum [42]

items.name: Scholze's functor from filtered flat bundles to B_dR^+-local systems, and de Rham local systems
items.statement: For S smooth over a p-adic field L, (V, ∇, Fil^•) ↦ M(V, ∇, Fil^•) = Fil^0(ν^{-1}V ⊗_{ν^{-1}O_{S_ét}} OB_dR)^{∇=0} is a fully faithful functor from filtered vector bundles with integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality ∇(Fil^i) ⊆ Fil^{i-1} ⊗ Ω^1_S to B_dR^+-local systems on S_proét; Fil^i V ⊗ Ô ≅ (Fil^i L ∩ M)/(Fil^i L ∩ Fil^1 M) (Scholze, Theorem 7.6, Lemma 7.8, Proposition 7.9), and R^1ν_*Ô(1) ≅ Ω^1_S (Scholze, Corollary 6.19). A Q_p-local system 𝕃 on S is de Rham if 𝕃 ⊗ B_dR^+ lies in the essential image of M (equivalently, Scholze's Definition 8.3); then the filtered flat bundle is recovered from 𝕃 and has underlying bundle ν_*(𝕃 ⊗ OB_dR).
items.locator: Section 2.5, p. 18; Theorem 3.3.1 and its proof, pp. 23–25; proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42; Section 10.1, pp. 62–63 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review note: Checked against Scholze's arXiv 1205.3463v2. Theorem 7.6 matches: M = Fil^0(E ⊗ OB_dR)^{∇=0} is a fully faithful functor to B_dR^+-local systems. Lemma 7.8, Proposition 7.9 and Corollary 6.19 also match. The item's 'Scholze's Definition 8.3' is the right number, but two caveats apply. First, Scholze's Definition 8.3 is stated only for proper smooth X, so the paper's Section 10.1 definition agrees with it only through Theorem 7.6. Second, the paper itself cites '[40, Definition 8.4]' on p. 42; this is recorded as a new misprint. Routing to PadicHodgeTheory P8 (route 5) is fine.

items.name: B_dR^+-local systems on the pro-étale site and on the diamond agree
items.statement: For S smooth over L, the category of B_dR^+-local systems on S_proét is equivalent to that of B_dR^+-local systems on S^♢ (both described, over an étale cover by toric charts with Galois perfectoid covers S̃_i = Spa(A_i, A_i^+), as finite projective B_dR^+(A_i)-modules with the same continuous semilinear descent data for Z_p(1)^n ⋊ Z_p^× and étale descent).

items.name: Hodge and Hodge–Tate analytic structures on basic local Shimura towers (minuscule case)
items.statement: Let [μ] be minuscule, b basic, M_C = M_{b,[μ]} ×_{Spd Q̆_p([μ])} Spd C, 𝔍 = Aut_cont(C/L([μ])). (1) The Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic Zariski topology on M_C is the inverse limit of the rigid analytic Zariski topologies on M_C/K (resp. M_C/K_b) for K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍 (resp. K_b ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍) compact open. (2) An irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set is a connected component of the preimage in M_C of an irreducible locally closed rigid subvariety of some M_C/K (resp. M_C/K_b). (3) A locally closed subdiamond is bi-analytic if it is both. (4) A special subvariety is a connected component of a subdiamond M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} for H ≤ G closed and [μ_H], b_H refining [μ], b up to σ-conjugation.
items.locator: Definition 1.1.2, p. 5; the Zariski topology on a rigid variety is recalled on p. 5
items.note: The general (non-minuscule) forms are Definitions 8.4.1 and 9.1.1, items 154 and 147.

items.name: The two limit presentations of a basic infinite-level moduli space
items.statement: Let [b] be the basic class in B(G, [μ^{-1}]), M_C = M_{b,[μ]} ×_{Spd Q̆_p([μ])} Spd C, and 𝔍 = Aut_cont(C/L([μ])). Then M_C = lim_K M_C/K over compact open K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍, and M_C = lim_{K_b} M_C/K_b over compact open K_b ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍. Both limits are along finite étale transition maps. The M_C/K are étale covers of Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ],L([μ])} via π_{L_ét}, and the M_C/K_b are étale covers of X_{[μ],L([μ])} via π_{L_dR}. For [μ] minuscule, Gr^{b-adm}_[μ] = Fl^{b-adm,♢}_{[μ^{-1}]} and X_[μ] is an open rigid subvariety of Fl_[μ]. In that case the finite levels are represented by smooth rigid analytic varieties over the finite extensions E = C^K of L([μ]). For G reductive they are the basic local Shimura varieties of Scholze–Weinstein; for the K_b tower this uses the duality of Theorem 8.5.1 (footnote 2).
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 5, Eq. (1.1.1.1) and footnote 2 (arXiv v2). The towers rest on Proposition 7.3.2, Lemma 8.3.1 and Theorem 8.5.1, and the étale maps M_C/K → Gr^{b-adm} are used in Section 9.2, p. 56
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item omits that both presentations are limits along finite étale transition maps; the paper says there are 'two natural presentations of M_C as a limit of finite étale maps'. It also omits that each M_C/K lies over Spd E, where E = C^K is a finite extension of L([μ]).

items.name: Algebraic sources of closed rigid subvarieties of finite-level spaces
items.statement: Let Y = M_C/K over Spd E, E = C^K. (1) If Z ⊆ Fl_{[μ^{-1}],E} is a closed algebraic subvariety, every irreducible component of its preimage under the Hodge period map Y → Fl^{b-adm}_{[μ^{-1}],E} is a closed rigid subvariety of Y. (2) If uniformization gives a map from Y to the basic locus of a global Shimura variety Sh/E, every irreducible component of the preimage of a closed algebraic Z ⊆ Sh is a closed rigid subvariety.

items.name: Special subvarieties from non-reductive subgroups exist even for reductive G
items.statement: Let G = GL_4, μ(z) = diag(z, z, 1, 1) (minuscule), and b basic. The local Shimura varieties for (G, [μ], b) are moduli spaces of certain two-dimensional height-four p-divisible formal groups. The standard parabolic H ≤ G with Levi subgroup GL_2 × GL_2, which is not reductive, gives a special subvariety. It classifies the formal groups that are extensions of one-dimensional height-two p-divisible formal groups, and non-trivial such extensions exist, as filtered isocrystals show. So special subvarieties attached to non-reductive subgroups occur even when G is reductive.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The label '(Lubin–Tate-type)' is the extraction's and is wrong. For G = GL_4, μ = (1,1,0,0) and b basic (isoclinic of slope 1/2), the local Shimura varieties classify two-dimensional height-four p-divisible formal groups. This is a basic Rapoport–Zink space of signature (2,2). A Lubin–Tate space has μ = (1,0,0,0). The paper says only 'moduli spaces of certain two-dimensional height four p-divisible formal groups'.

items.name: Theorem A(1): the minuscule bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear algebraic, [μ] minuscule with a basic class [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), L/Q̆_p a complete discretely valued extension with algebraically closed residue field, C = L̄^ and M_C = M_{b,[μ],C}. The Hodge–Tate (resp. Hodge) analytic Zariski closure of an irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set in M_C is a special subvariety.
items.locator: Theorem A, p. 6; proved as the minuscule case of Theorem 9.1.3
items.note: Review note: Statement matches Theorem A and §1.1, p. 3 (L complete and discretely valued with algebraically closed residue field κ; Q̆_p = W(F̄_p)[1/p] ⊆ L; 𝔍 = Aut_cont(C/L([μ]))). The deduction from Theorem 9.1.3 also needs Remark 9.1.2 (in the minuscule case the closures of Definition 9.1.1 are the closures for the inverse-limit Zariski topology of Definition 1.1.2, item 041) and Remark 8.4.3 (the three notions of special agree when [μ] is minuscule). The empty-index case of Theorem 9.1.3(2) cannot occur here: every M_C/K_b is rigid analytic, so the connected component through π_{K_b}(Z̃) is a closed rigid analytic subdiamond containing it. Theorem A uses a strict field, so the new gaps about non-strict L (Lemma 9.3.5, and Part I Corollary 5.5.3 in the proof of 9.1.3) do not affect it.

items.name: Theorem A(2): special subvarieties are the only closed bi-analytic sets
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem A, special subvarieties are the only closed bi-analytic sets in M_C.

items.name: Ax–Lindemann for algebraic conditions on the Hodge–Tate flag variety
items.statement: Let Z' be an algebraic subvariety of Fl_{[μ],L([μ])} and Z an irreducible component of the rigid variety Z'_C ∩ X_{[μ],C}. Then any connected component Z̃ of π_HT^{-1}(Z) is an irreducible Hodge–Tate analytic set, and the rigid analytic Zariski closure of its image in the finite-level local Shimura variety M_{b,[μ],C}/K is a finite-level special subvariety.

items.name: The zero-dimensional case of Theorem A is Part I's characterization of special points
items.statement: The characterization of the zero-dimensional bi-analytic subvarieties in Theorem A (and in Theorem 9.1.3 in the non-minuscule case) is equivalent to Part I, Corollary C.

items.name: Hyperbolic Ax–Lindemann for Shimura varieties (Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev)
items.statement: Let (G, X^+) be a connected Shimura datum, J: X^+ → Sh_G°(C) = Γ\X^+ the uniformization and X^+ ⊆ Fl_G(C) the period embedding. If Z ⊆ Fl_G is a complex algebraic subvariety and Z_0 an analytic irreducible component of Z(C) ∩ X^+, then the algebraic Zariski closure of J(Z_0) in Sh_G°(C) is a weakly special subvariety. In particular the C-bi-algebraic subvarieties are exactly the weakly special subvarieties.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2.3, p. 8; quoted from Klingler–Ullmo–Yafaev 2016, in the formulation of their survey, Theorem 4.28, for comparison

items.name: Neutral admissible pairs over a strict p-adic field are admissible pairs with good reduction
items.statement: Let L be a p-adic field with algebraically closed residue field and C = L̄^. A neutral admissible pair over Spd L is the same as an admissible pair (W, L_ét) over C with good reduction over L in the sense of Part I Definition 5.4.1, i.e. L_ét = L_can(Fil^•) for a filtration Fil^• on W_L. The reason: Spd L = Spd L̄^/Gal(L̄/L), and the lattices on W ⊗ B_dR that come from filtrations over L are exactly the Gal(L̄/L)-stable ones (Part I Proposition 3.1.7(2) and Example 3.1.10), i.e. those that descend to Spd L.
items.locator: Example 1.3.1, p. 10 (arXiv v2), citing Part I Definition 5.4.1 (printed as 'I.Section 5.5')
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item follows the paper's 'I.Section 5.5', but Part I defines admissible pairs with good reduction over a strict p-adic subfield in Definition 5.4.1 (Section 5.4). Section 5.5 attaches Galois representations to them. The paper's misprint is recorded as a new issue.

items.name: Theorem B(1): generic motivic Galois group and lattice type over a rigid variety
items.statement: Let L be a strict p-adic field (so Q̆_p ⊆ L), Z/Spa L a geometrically irreducible rigid analytic variety and A = (W, L_ét) a neutral admissible pair on Z^♢. Fix a geometric point x of Z, set G := MG(A, x) (Definition 7.2.1), and fix ω_x∘A ≅ ω_std, so that A becomes a neutral G-admissible pair through its canonical reduction of structure group. Then this G-admissible pair has a type [μ] (Definition 7.2.2; Theorem 7.2.3 applied to the seminormalization of Z), a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} that is Galois-stable and hence defined over L. By Lemmas 9.3.1 and 9.3.3, G is also the motivic Galois group at a dense set of classical points (the Hodge generic ones).
items.locator: Theorem B, p. 11; proof in Section 9.2, p. 58 (the type from Theorem 7.2.3; Lemma 9.3.1 enters only in part (2))
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Faithful to p. 11, but the terms 'generic motivic Galois group' and 'good with lattice invariant [μ]' are defined nowhere in Part II. The proof on p. 58 shows what they mean: G = MG(A, x) (Definition 7.2.1), and the lattice invariant is the type of Definition 7.2.2, obtained from Theorem 7.2.3. Theorem 7.2.3 also needs Z seminormal, which costs nothing because Z^♢ = (Z^sn)^♢.

items.name: Theorem B(2): density of the Hodge–Tate period image
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem B(1), let C = L̄^, Z̃ → Z_C^♢ a geometric connected component of the associated G(Q_p)-torsor over Z^♢ and π_HT: Z̃ → Fl^♢_{[μ],L([μ])} its Hodge–Tate period map. Then π_HT(Z̃) is rigid Zariski dense in every connected open of Fl^♢_{[μ],L([μ])} that it meets.
items.locator: Theorem B, p. 11; proved in Section 9.2, p. 58
items.note: Review note: Matches p. 11. The proof on p. 58 reruns the argument for Theorem 9.1.3(2) with f the inclusion into a connected open U of Fl_{[μ],L([μ])}. It needs a Hodge generic classical point z with π_HT(z̃) ∈ U, which exists because Z̃ → Z_C^♢ is open. It also needs the closed rigid subsets to be defined over a finite extension of L([μ]), so that they are stable under an open subgroup of Galois.

items.name: Filtered O-local systems and their types
items.statement: Let X/Spd Q_p be a locally spatial diamond. A filtered O-local system is an O-local system V with a decreasing filtration F^•V by O-local subsystems such that gr^•V = ⊕_i F^iV/F^{i+1}V is an O-local system and, at each geometric point x, x^*F^iV = 0 for i ≫ 0 and = x^*V for i ≪ 0. The filtration is then locally finite by local direct summands, and its type (the multiset of i counted with rank gr^i) is a locally constant function on |X|. For G = GL_n and μ = (t^{i_1}, …, t^{i_n}) the type is [μ] exactly when rank gr^i V is the multiplicity of i in {i_1, …, i_n} (Example 3.0.2).

items.name: Lattices, latticed B_dR^+-local systems and bilatticed B_dR-local systems
items.statement: For a B_dR-local system V on X, a lattice is a B_dR^+-submodule L ⊆ V that is a B_dR^+-local system with L ⊗ B_dR = V. A latticed B_dR^+-local system is (M, L) with M a B_dR^+-local system and L ⊆ M ⊗ B_dR a lattice; a bilatticed B_dR-local system is (V, L_1, L_2) with two lattices. The two notions are equivalent by M ⊗ B_dR = L ⊗ B_dR ↔ V, M ↔ L_1, L ↔ L_2; Loc^bl_{B_dR}(X) denotes the bilatticed ones.

items.name: The type of a bilatticed B_dR-local system
items.statement: If X = Spa(C, C^+) with C algebraically closed, B_dR^+(C) is a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field C, and the type of a bilatticed B_dR(C)-vector space is the multiset of integers giving the elementary divisors of L_2 relative to L_1 (for GL_n: (M, L) has type (t^{i_1}, …, t^{i_n}) if M has a basis e_j with ξ^{i_j}e_j a basis of L, Example 3.0.1). For general X the type at geometric points is a function on |X|, which need not be locally constant.

items.name: The type of a bilatticed family need not be locally constant
items.statement: On the closed disc D = Spa C_p⟨z⟩ the bilatticed B_dR-module (B_dR^2, (B_dR^+)^2, B_dR^+ e_1 + B_dR^+(e_2 + (z/ξ)e_1)) is well defined (the lattice on the perfectoid cover Spa C_p⟨z^{1/p^∞}⟩ built from [(z, z^{1/p}, …)] is invariant under the covering group because (1 − ε)/ξ ∈ B_dR^+) and has type {1, −1} for z ≠ 0 and type {0, 0} at z = 0.
items.note: Review note: Checked: for z ≠ 0 the basis ξe_2, ξ^{-1}(e_1 + (ξ/z)e_2) of the second lattice is ξf_1, ξ^{-1}f_2 with (f_1, f_2) = (e_2, e_1 + (ξ/z)e_2) a basis of (B_dR^+)^2 (determinant −1), so the type is {1, −1}. The invariance computation τ(e_2 + (z̃/ξ)e_1) = e_2 + (z̃/ξ)e_1 − z̃((1−ε)/ξ)e_1 is correct.

items.name: The trace filtration and the Bialynicki-Birula functors
items.statement: For a latticed B_dR^+-local system (M, L), trFil^i_L(M ⊗_{B_dR^+} O) := image of (Fil^i B_dR · L) ∩ M in M ⊗ O ≅ ((Fil^i B_dR·L) ∩ M)/((Fil^i B_dR·L) ∩ (Fil^1 B_dR·M)) is a filtration by O-submodules. It gives functors BB_1(V, L_1, L_2) = (L_1 ⊗ O, trFil_{L_2}) and BB_2(V, L_1, L_2) = (L_2 ⊗ O, trFil_{L_1}) from Loc^bl_{B_dR}(X) to O-local systems with a filtration by O-submodules.

items.name: Constant type gives a filtration by local direct summands
items.statement: If a bilatticed B_dR-local system has constant type on X, its trace filtrations are by local direct summands, so BB_1 and BB_2 land in filtered O-local systems; BB_1 inverts the type and BB_2 preserves it (the argument of Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 19.4.2). Example 3.1.1 shows that without constant type the graded pieces need not be local systems.
items.locator: Section 3.1, p. 21 (the paragraph after Eq. (3.1.1.1)) (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review note: Missing confirmed: no stage plans the Bialynicki-Birula map or Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 19.4.2 / Caraiani–Scholze Proposition 3.4.3 (searched 'Bialynicki|trace filtration|19.4.2'). Checked the type bookkeeping: if L_2 has basis ξ^{i_j}e_j, then trFil^k_{L_2}(L_1 ⊗ O) is spanned by the e_j with −i_j ≥ k, so BB_1 has type {−i_j} and BB_2 type {i_j}.

items.name: The graded pieces of the two trace filtrations differ by a Tate twist
items.statement: For (V, L_1, L_2) ∈ Loc^bl_{B_dR}(X) and V_i = L_i ⊗_{B_dR^+} O, for each i ∈ Z multiplication induces gr^i_{L_2} V_1 ≅ gr^{-i}_{L_1} V_2(i), where (i) is the tensor product with gr^i B_dR = O ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(i).
items.note: Review note: Checked: gr^i_{L_2}V_1 = (ξ^iL_2 ∩ L_1)/(ξ^{i+1}L_2 ∩ L_1 + ξ^iL_2 ∩ ξL_1), and multiplication by ξ^{-i} carries it isomorphically onto gr^{-i}_{L_1}V_2. The canonical map is gr^{-i}_{L_1}V_2 ⊗ gr^iB_dR → gr^i_{L_2}V_1, which gives the twist (i). The printed proof has 'tL_1' for ξL_1 (E2).

items.name: Filtered, latticed and bilatticed G-local systems and their types
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic and X/Spd L a locally spatial diamond. A filtered G(O)-local system is an exact tensor functor from Rep G to filtered O-local systems (sending exact sequences to strict exact sequences); latticed G(B_dR^+)- and bilatticed G(B_dR)-local systems are defined likewise and are equivalent (two G(B_dR^+)-local systems with an isomorphism of their push-outs to G(B_dR)). A filtered G(O)-local system has a locally constant type [μ] with values in Gal(L̄/L)-orbits of conjugacy classes of cocharacters; a bilatticed one has a type function, with an extra value ∅ (no type) when G is not reductive, which may not be locally constant; it is good of type [ν] if this function is constant equal to [ν].

items.name: A bilatticed G-local system is good of type [μ] iff its trace filtrations are filtered G-local systems
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic, [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{L̄}, X a diamond over Spd L([μ]) and 𝒢^bl a bilatticed G(B_dR)-local system on X. The following are equivalent: (1) 𝒢^bl is good of type [μ]; (2) BB_1∘𝒢^bl is a filtered G(O)-local system of type [μ^{-1}]; (3) BB_2∘𝒢^bl is a filtered G(O)-local system of type [μ].
items.note: The proof reduces to geometric points (Part I, Theorem 3.2.6, item 006) and argues as in Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 19.4.2 over affinoid perfectoids. Review note: Statement checked against the image. The proof's parenthetical 'for any representation of V' is a misprint for 'any representation V of G' (new issue). The note's reference (Part I Theorem 3.2.6 = theorem.good-equivalence-bilatticed) agrees with the Part I TeX.

items.name: Semicontinuity of the type, and its failure for non-reductive groups
items.statement: For G reductive, the type of a bilatticed G(B_dR)-local system is lower semicontinuous for the Bruhat order (Scholze–Weinstein, Proposition 19.2.3, after trivializing one lattice). For general G, once the type of the push-out to the Levi quotient is fixed, the locus where a type exists is closed (so ∅ is an open point), but declaring ∅ maximal does not make the type lower semicontinuous: Example 7.5.10 has a type on an open locus and none on its closed complement.
items.note: Review note: The reductive half (closedness of the Schubert varieties Gr_{≤μ}, Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 19.2.3) is planned by GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:loop-geometry ('construct Schubert cells/closures … closure relations'), so cite it for that half. The non-reductive half (the type ∅ and Example 7.5.10) is new and belongs to route 1.

items.name: The trivial-filtration lattice M_0 of a flat bundle
items.statement: For (V, ∇) a vector bundle with integrable connection on a smooth rigid variety X over L, M_0(V, ∇) := M(V, ∇, Fil_triv), Fil_triv^i V = V for i ≤ 0 and 0 for i > 0; it is the extension to the v-site of (ν^{-1}V ⊗ OB_dR^+)^{∇=0}, and the a priori inclusion (ν^{-1}V ⊗ OB_dR^+)^{∇=0} ⊆ (ν^{-1}V ⊗ Fil^0 OB_dR)^{∇=0} is an equality. For every Griffiths-transversal filtration, M(V, ∇, Fil^•) is a B_dR^+-lattice in M_0(V, ∇) ⊗ B_dR.
items.note: Review note: The item rightly says '(V, ∇) a vector bundle with integrable connection'. The paper's 'filtered vector bundle' at this point is a slip (new issue).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.1(1): flat bundles embed into B_dR^+-local systems
items.statement: For X/Spa L smooth, (V, ∇) ↦ M_0(V, ∇) is a fully faithful functor from vector bundles with integrable connection on X to B_dR^+-local systems on X^♢, and v_*(M_0(V, ∇) ⊗_{B_dR^+} O) = V under (X^♢_ét, O|_{X^♢_ét}) = (X_ét, O_{X_ét}).

items.name: Theorem 3.3.1(2): Griffiths-transversal filtered flat bundles embed into latticed B_dR^+-local systems
items.statement: (V, ∇, Fil^•) ↦ (M_0(V, ∇), L_Fil), L_Fil := M(V, ∇, Fil^•) ⊆ M_0(V, ∇) ⊗ B_dR, is a fully faithful tensor functor from filtered vector bundles with integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality on X to latticed B_dR^+-local systems on X^♢; under (1) the pushforward along v of the trace filtration of L_Fil is Fil^•, and L_Fil is the unique lattice with this property.

items.name: Theorem 3.3.1(3): the essential image is the constant-type locus
items.statement: Let L be a p-adic field and X/Spa L a smooth rigid analytic variety. A latticed B_dR^+-local system (M, L) on X^♢ lies in the essential image of the functor of (2) if and only if M lies in the essential image of M_0 and the trace filtration (3.1.1.1) of L on M ⊗_{B_dR^+} O is by local direct summands. Equivalently, M is in the essential image of M_0 and the type of L is locally constant on |X^♢|. In that case, writing M = M_0(V, ∇), there is a filtration Fil^• of V by local direct summands on X_ét whose pullback to O is the trace filtration. This filtration satisfies Griffiths transversality, and L = M(V, ∇, Fil^•).
items.locator: Theorem 3.3.1(3), p. 24 (arXiv v2); proof pp. 24–25, by induction on r_1 − r_n using Caraiani–Scholze Proposition 3.4.3, Scholze Corollary 6.19 and Lemma 7.8, and the proof of Scholze Proposition 7.9 (the uniqueness Lemma 7.10)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The parenthetical '(equivalently, the type of L is constant)' copies a slip. For disconnected X, a lattice whose type is constant on each connected component, but different on different components, has a trace filtration by local direct summands and lies in the essential image. The equivalence holds with 'locally constant'. Separately, the printed proof leaves out the descent of the trace filtration from O-modules on X_proét to X_ét (new gap issue); the statement stays true.

items.name: Scholze's functor over a p-adic field
items.statement: For X = Spd L the connection is trivial and (V, Fil^•) ↦ M(V, Fil^•) sends filtered L-vector spaces to Gal(L̄/L)-semilinear B_dR^+(C)-modules (C = L̄^); its essential image is the modules M with dim_L (M ⊗ B_dR(C))^{Gal(L̄/L)} = rank M, and M_0 = (M ⊗ B_dR(C))^{Gal(L̄/L)} ⊗_L B_dR^+(C) is recovered from M.

items.name: Isocrystals, their Dieudonné–Manin classification and the associated bundles
items.statement: Isocrystals (finite-dimensional Q̆_p-vector spaces W with a σ-semilinear bijection φ_W) form an exact Q_p-linear tensor category. It is semisimple, with simple objects classified by their slope (Dieudonné–Manin). For S ∈ Perf_{F̄_p}, an isocrystal W gives a vector bundle 𝓔(W) on FF_S by descending W ⊗_{Q̆_p} O_{Y_S} along φ_W ⊗ φ. This is exact, compatible with tensor products and natural in S. The slopes of 𝓔(W) are the negatives of the slopes of W.
items.locator: Section 4.1, p. 26; Section 6.2, p. 37 (the sign of slopes)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The functor is garbled as 'E ↦ E(W)'. The paper writes 𝓔(W) for the bundle attached to an isocrystal W (e.g. Section 7.1: 'the vector bundle 𝓔(W)'). Review note: Planned confirmed: VB0 plans isocrystals and Dieudonné–Manin, and asks to 'compute the slope of its associated bundle and record any sign reversal explicitly'. VB1 plans the isocrystal-to-bundle functor and its comparison under S-base change.

items.name: G-isocrystals, B(G) and basic classes for connected linear algebraic G
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, a G-isocrystal is an exact tensor functor Rep G → Isoc; b ∈ G(Q̆_p) gives V ↦ (V ⊗ Q̆_p, ρ(b)(id ⊗ σ)), inducing a bijection between B(G) (σ-conjugacy classes) and isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals. b is basic if its slope morphism ν_b (Kottwitz) factors through the centre of G; then ν_b is independent of the representative and defined over Q_p, and b is basic if and only if the adjoint isocrystal on Lie G is trivial. B(G)_basic ⊆ B(G) is the set of basic classes.
items.note: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0 and BG1 plan G-isocrystals, B(G), Newton points and basic classes for reductive G; the non-reductive definitions are new. Review note: Missing is right for non-reductive G. BG0 (B(G) as σ-conjugacy classes, compared with G-isocrystals) and BG1 (Newton points, basic classes) plan only the reductive case, as the note says. For non-reductive G, the bijection between B(G) and G-isocrystals uses Steinberg's theorem H^1(Q̆_p, G) = 0 (Part I §2.2.3). No stage plans that theorem (see coverage).

items.name: Levi decompositions and B(G): basic in G versus basic in M
items.statement: If G = MU is a Levi decomposition, the inclusion M → G induces B(G) = B(M) with inverse induced by G → M. A basic class of B(G) gives a basic class of B(M), but not conversely: for G the upper-triangular Borel of GL_2 and M the diagonal torus, b = diag(p, 1) is basic in M but not in G (Part I Example 2.2.4).
items.note: Review note: Checked against Part I §2.2.3 (B(G) = B(G/U), B(G)_basic ⊆ B(M)_basic) and Part I Example 2.2.4 (b = diag(p,1) in the upper-triangular Borel of GL_2), whose numbering matches the Part I TeX.

items.name: The σ-centralizer group G_b
items.statement: For b ∈ G(Q̆_p), G_b(R) = Aut^⊗ of the extension of scalars to Isoc ⊗_{Q_p} R of the G-isocrystal of b; G_b is a linear algebraic group over Q_p with G_b(Q_p) the σ-centralizer of b in G(Q̆_p) (Rapoport–Zink, Proposition 1.12). For b basic, G_b is an inner form of G and G(Q̆_p) = G_b(Q̆_p) canonically.
items.note: BG0 constructs J_b = G_b for reductive G. Review note: BG0 constructs J_b = G_b for reductive G. The non-reductive case (Rapoport–Zink Proposition 1.12; inner form when b is basic, via Part I §2.2.3) is new.

items.name: Bun_G for a connected linear algebraic group G
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, Bun_G is the prestack on Perf_{F̄_p} sending S to the groupoid of G-bundles on FF_S (in any of the equivalent forms of Fargues–Scholze, Definition/Proposition III.1.1); it is a small v-stack (the reductive argument does not use reductivity). For b ∈ G(Q̆_p), E_b: Spd F̄_p → Bun_G is the descent of the trivial G-bundle on Y_S along bσ; Tannakianly, the G-isocrystal of b followed by Isoc → Vect(FF_S).
items.note: BunGAndNewtonStrata BG2:uniformization defines Bun_G for reductive G. Review note: BG2:uniformization defines Bun_G for reductive G and proves v-descent and smallness. The paper's remark that the argument does not use reductivity makes the non-reductive definition a small addition for route 1. Checked Fargues–Scholze Proposition III.1.3 ('The v-stack Bun_G is small'); the paper misprints its number as III.I.3 (new issue).

items.name: Automorphisms of E_b and the classifying-stack map
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf_{F̄_p}, the sheaf of sections of G_b × FF_S maps into the automorphism sheaf of E_b on (FF_S)_ét, isomorphically for b basic; since global sections of G_b × FF_S are Cont(|S|, G_b(Q_p)), E_b induces a faithful map [∗/G_b(Q_p)] → Bun_G which is full when b is basic. (Fullness fails in general; the image of b in G/U being basic is necessary but not sufficient.)

items.name: Theorem 4.2.2(1): basic strata of Bun_G are classifying stacks
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear algebraic. For each [b] ∈ B(G)_basic, the substack Bun_G^{[b]} (G-bundles geometrically isomorphic to E_b) is an open substack of Bun_G, and for any b ∈ [b] the map E_b is an isomorphism [∗/G_b(Q_p)] ≅ Bun_G^{[b]}.
items.note: For G reductive this is Fargues–Scholze Theorem III.4.5, planned in BunGAndNewtonStrata BG3. Review note: BG3 plans the reductive case (for basic b, the classifying-stack description by J_b(E), and openness of the basic locus), as the note says. The non-reductive extension is new (route 1). Proof checked: the openness and the v-cover property come from (4.2.2.2) and the reductive case for M, and full faithfulness comes from Aut(E_b) ≅ G_b × FF_S for b basic.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.2(2): basic strata are pulled back from the Levi quotient
items.statement: With M = G/U the reductive quotient and [b_M] the image of [b] in B(M), Bun_G^{[b]} ≅ Bun_G ×_{Bun_M} Bun_M^{[b_M]} (push-out of bundles along G → M). The proof shows that every object of the right side is v-locally isomorphic to E_b, by killing the class in H^1_ét(FF_S, 𝒰) (𝒰 an inner form of U) pro-étale locally, inductively along the derived series of U.
items.note: Review note: Proof checked. For [b] basic in G, Ad(b) has slope 0 on Lie G, hence on every quotient in the derived series of Lie U. So the twisted unipotent group 𝒰 has trivial vector bundles as graded pieces, and nonabelian H^1 classes die pro-étale locally by induction (the fibre of H^1(𝒰) → H^1(𝒰/𝒰^{(1)}) over the trivial class is the image of H^1(𝒰^{(1)})). 'Basic in G', not merely in M, is essential (E14). The proof also uses the fact that commutative unipotent groups are G-equivariantly vector groups, which no item covers (see coverage).

items.name: Cohomology of O on the relative curve
items.statement: H^1_ét(FF_S, O) = H^1(FF_S, O) (Kedlaya–Liu, Theorem 8.2.22(c)), and classes in H^1(FF_S, O) are killed pro-étale locally on S (Fargues–Scholze, Proposition II.2.5(ii)).
items.note: Review note: VB2:ampleness does not plan this: it treats positive twists, global generation and algebraization. VB1 plans H^0 and H^1 of bundles and descent, but no stage names Fargues–Scholze Proposition II.2.5(ii) (E ≅ BC(O) as pro-étale sheaves; the pro-étale sheafification of S ↦ H^1(X_S, O) vanishes) or Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 8.2.22(c). The nearest stages are VB3:general-BC ('for degree-zero pieces identify the locally profinite E-vector-space behavior') and VB4 (slope-zero bundles as pro-étale local systems, whose proof uses II.2.5(ii)). Suggest planned = [VB1, VB3:general-BC, VB4], with a request that these stages state II.2.5(ii) and Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22(c) explicitly. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): planned stages changed from VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB2:ampleness to VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB1, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB3:general-BC, VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4. VB2:ampleness treats positive twists, global generation and algebraization, not this. VB3:general-BC (degree-zero pieces) and VB4 (slope-zero bundles as pro-étale local systems) are the nearest stages; they should state Fargues–Scholze II.2.5(ii) and Kedlaya–Liu 8.2.22(c) explicitly.

items.name: Bun_G of an inner twist by a basic class
items.statement: For b ∈ G(Q̆_p) basic, 𝓔 ↦ Isom_{FF_S}(E_b, 𝓔) is an equivalence F_b: Bun_G ≅ Bun_{G_b} (as in Fargues–Scholze III.4.1).
items.locator: Section 4.2, p. 28 (the paragraph before Lemma 4.2.3; the notation a_G, a_{G_b} is on p. 29) (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review note: BG0 plans inner twisting of torsors for reductive G (Fargues–Scholze Proposition III.4.1). Fargues–Scholze Corollary III.4.3 (Bun_G ≃ Bun_{G_b}) is not named in BG3. Missing is right for non-reductive G.

items.name: Twisting exchanges the trivial and basic bundles
items.statement: Writing a_G, a_{G_b} for a ∈ G(Q̆_p) = G_b(Q̆_p), there are natural isomorphisms in Bun_{G_b}(Spd F̄_p): F_b(E_{b_G}) ≅ E_{1_{G_b}} and F_b(E_{1_G}) ≅ E_{b^{-1}_{G_b}}.
items.note: Review note: Checked. On Y_S, Isom(E_b, E_1) is the trivial torsor with Frobenius g ↦ σ(g)b^{-1} = b^{-1}σ_b(g), where σ_b = Ad(b)∘σ is the Frobenius of G_b(Q̆_p) = G(Q̆_p). This is E_{b^{-1}} for G_b, matching the lemma.

items.name: Modifications of G-bundles at the untilt
items.statement: For S ∈ Perf over Spd Q̆_p with untilt ∞: S^♯ → FF_S (a closed Cartier divisor whose completed local ring is B_dR^+), completion gives an exact tensor functor Vect(FF_S) → Loc_{B_dR^+}(S); for E ∈ Bun_G(S) and a lattice L on the G(B_dR)-local system E|_{B_dR}, Beauville–Laszlo gluing gives the modification E_L ∈ Bun_G(S), functorially, interpolating the modifications at geometric points.
items.note: RF4 plans Beauville–Laszlo gluing for vector bundles and its Tannakian transfer to G-torsors (for the reductive groups of BG0); the paper's Tannakian reduction to vector bundles applies to any linear algebraic G. Review note: Planned confirmed: RF4:vector-bundles (Beauville–Laszlo gluing along the Cartier divisors) and RF4:G-torsors (Tannakian transfer; the paper's reduction to vector bundles works for any linear algebraic G). Add RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts, which constructs the untilt divisor and completion along it (B_dR^+). The item uses this input ('the completion of O_{FF_S} at I_∞ is B_dR^+', Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 11.3.1). Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): planned stages changed from RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles, RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:G-torsors to RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:vector-bundles, RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF4:G-torsors, RelativeFarguesFontaine:RF2:untilts. RF2:untilts constructs the untilt divisor and the completion along it (B_dR^+), which the item uses.

items.name: The B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian and the flag variety of a connected linear algebraic group
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic (L a p-adic field). Gr_G/Spd L is the functor on Perfd_L sending X to isomorphism classes of lattices on the trivial G(B_dR)-local system (equivalently on the trivial G(B_dR^+)-local system); Fl_G/Spa L is the rigid variety whose points on adic spaces X/Spa L are filtrations on the trivial G-bundle on X_ét, and Fl_G^♢ parameterizes filtrations on the trivial G(O)-local system.
items.locator: Definition 5.0.1, first list (1)–(2), pp. 29–30 (arXiv v2; the definition begins at the foot of p. 29, its content is on p. 30)
items.note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0:loop-geometry plans the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannians for reductive G. Review note: missing is right for general connected G. For reductive G the B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian (the one-leg case of the Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian) is planned in GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:loop-geometry, which the new roadmap should import. No atlas stage plans the p-adic flag variety Fl_G for non-reductive G.

items.name: Affine Schubert cells, flag varieties of type [μ] and the Bialynicki-Birula map
items.statement: For [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{L̄} with reflex field L([μ]): Gr_[μ] ⊆ Gr_G ×_{Spd L} Spd L([μ]) parameterizes lattices of type [μ] (at C-points: L(V) = μ(ξ)V_{B_dR^+(C)} for some μ ∈ [μ]_{B_dR^+(C)} and a generator ξ of Fil^1 B_dR^+(C)); Fl_[μ] ⊆ Fl_G ×_{Spa L} Spa L([μ]) parameterizes filtrations of type [μ] (Fil^i V_C = ⊕_{j≥i} V_C[j] for some μ ∈ [μ]_C); and BB: Gr_[μ] → Fl^♢_[μ^{-1}] sends a lattice to its trace filtration (well defined by Theorem 3.2.1). G(B_dR^+) preserves Gr_[μ] and BB is G(B_dR^+)-equivariant.
items.locator: Definition 5.0.1, second list (1)–(3), p. 30; Remark 5.0.2 and the paragraph after it (the G(B_dR)-action; Gr_[μ] is G(B_dR^+)-stable; BB is G(B_dR^+)-equivariant), p. 30 (arXiv v2)

items.name: Torsor and coset descriptions of Gr_G
items.statement: (1) For X = Spa(A, A^+) affinoid perfectoid, Gr_G(X) is the set of G-torsors on Spec B_dR^+(A) trivialized over Spec B_dR(A). (2) Gr_G is the étale (or v) sheafification of X ↦ G(B_dR(X))/G(B_dR^+(X)); for C algebraically closed, Gr_G(C) = G(B_dR(C))/G(B_dR^+(C)) and, over L([μ]), Gr_[μ](C) = G(B_dR^+(C)) ξ^μ G(B_dR^+(C))/G(B_dR^+(C)).
items.locator: Proposition 5.0.3(1)–(2), pp. 30–31 (arXiv v2; the heading is at the foot of p. 30, the parts are on p. 31)
items.note: Review note: missing is right for general G. For reductive G, GS0:loop-geometry plans the torsor interpretation and the loop-group quotient LG/L^+G.

items.name: Gr_G is a v-sheaf
items.statement: Gr_G is a v-sheaf, and for any diamond X, Gr_G(X) is the set of isomorphism classes of lattices on the trivial G(B_dR)- (equivalently G(B_dR^+)-) local system on X_v (lattices on the trivial local system have no automorphisms).

items.name: Maps from rigid varieties to flag varieties; Fl_[μ] is clopen
items.statement: For S/Spa L seminormal rigid, Hom(S^♢, Fl_G^♢) is the set of filtrations on the trivial G-bundle on S_ét; Fl_[μ] ⊆ Fl_G ×_L Spa L([μ]) is a clopen subvariety.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(1): Gr_G is separated, partially proper and ind-(closed locally spatial)
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic with unipotent radical U and reductive quotient M. Gr_G is separated and partially proper over Spd L and an increasing union of closed locally spatial subdiamonds.
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31; part (1), proved in Section 5.1
items.note: The proof embeds G as an observable subgroup of a reductive G' (item 020) and applies Lemma 5.1.1 with the reductive case (Scholze–Weinstein Lecture 19; GS0:loop-geometry). Review note: missing is right. The reductive input (Gr_{G'} separated and an increasing union of closed spatial Gr_{≤μ}) is GS0:loop-geometry; the new roadmap should cite it rather than re-plan it.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(2): Schubert cells are locally closed, and closed when minuscule on the Levi
items.statement: Gr_[μ] ⊆ Gr_G ×_{Spd L} Spd L([μ]) is a locally closed locally spatial subdiamond, partially proper over Spd L([μ]); if [μ]_M is minuscule (weights of Ad∘μ on Lie M in {−1, 0, 1}) it is closed.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(3): Gr_[μ] is closed in the preimage of the Levi Schubert cell
items.statement: Gr_[μ] is a closed subdiamond of Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M}.
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31; part (3), proved as Proposition 5.2.1

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(4): maps from rigid varieties see only the Schubert cell, and are Griffiths-transversal filtrations
items.statement: If S/Spa L([μ]) is a seminormal rigid analytic variety, then (Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M})(S^♢) = Gr_[μ](S^♢), and BB induces a bijection between this set and the filtrations in Fl_[μ^{-1}](S) satisfying Griffiths transversality over the smooth locus S^sm for the trivial connection on the trivial G-bundle.
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4, p. 31; part (4), Eq. (5.0.4.1), p. 31; proved in Section 5.3
items.note: Proof: classical points (Part I Proposition 3.1.7(2)), density of classical points and closedness (3); for smooth S, Theorem 3.3.1; in general a resolution of singularities (Temkin) and v-descent.

items.name: Theorem 5.0.4(5): BB is an isomorphism exactly when the weights are at most one
items.statement: Let G/L be connected linear algebraic and [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{L̄}. If the weights of [μ] for the adjoint action on Lie G are ≤ 1, then BB: Gr_[μ] → Fl^♢_[μ^{-1}] is an isomorphism. If some weight of [μ] on Lie G is > 1, then the universal filtration on Fl_[μ^{-1}] fails Griffiths transversality for the trivial connection on every non-empty open subset: a root subgroup of weight > 1 for μ gives a non-transversal direction at Fil_{μ^{-1}}. Hence BB has no section over any non-empty open of Fl^♢_[μ^{-1}] (by part (4)), and in particular is not an isomorphism. (For G reductive the first assertion is [SW, Proposition 19.4.2]; the bijection on points is Part I Proposition 3.1.7(1).)
items.locator: Theorem 5.0.4(5), p. 32 (the theorem begins on p. 31; part (5) is printed on p. 32); proof in Section 5.3, p. 35 (arXiv v2)
items.note: For G reductive and μ minuscule this is Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem 19.4.2; the bijection on points is Part I Proposition 3.1.7(1). Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Two small points. (a) 'over no open subset' should read 'over no non-empty open subset' (the empty open trivially satisfies it). The consequence is that BB has no section over any non-empty open of Fl^♢_[μ^{-1}], since such a section would contradict part (4) on that open. (b) The note cites 'Scholze–Weinstein, Theorem 19.4.2'. The paper cites it as [SW, Proposition 19.4.2] (TeX, Sections 3.1–3.2).

items.name: The affine Grassmannian of the additive group
