items.statement: For G = G_a the only cocharacter is trivial and Gr_[μ_triv] = Spd L is the trivial lattice, while Gr_G = B_dR/B_dR^+ = ∪_n t^{-n}B_dR^+/B_dR^+ is enormous; its only rigid analytic point over Spd L is 0, so every map from a rigid analytic diamond to Gr_{G_a} is constant at 0.

items.name: Push-out along a closed subgroup embeds affine Grassmannians
items.statement: Let G' be connected linear algebraic over L and G ≤ G' closed. The push-out Gr_G → Gr_{G'} is injective; if G'/G is quasi-affine it identifies Gr_G with a Zariski locally closed subdiamond of Gr_{G'}, and if G'/G is affine with a Zariski closed one.

items.name: The Bruhat order on conjugacy classes of cocharacters
items.statement: For G with reductive quotient M, choose T ⊆ B ⊆ M_{L̄}; each [μ]_M has a unique B-dominant representative in X_*(T), and [μ_1] ≥ [μ_2] if μ_1 − μ_2 is a non-negative integral combination of B-positive coroots (independent of T and B). Gr_{≤[μ]} (types ≤ [μ] at every geometric point) is closed and proper over Spd L([μ]) for G reductive (Scholze–Weinstein Proposition 19.2.3), so Gr_[μ] is open in Gr_{≤[μ]} and closed when [μ] is minuscule.
items.locator: Section 5.2, pp. 33–34 (arXiv v2): the Bruhat order on p. 33; Gr_{≤[μ]}, [SW, Proposition 19.2.3] and the minuscule case on p. 34
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry plans bounded Schubert cells, closures, properness and closure relations for reductive G; for general G the order is taken on the reductive quotient. Review note: planned is right for the reductive part: GS0:loop-geometry plans bounded Schubert diamonds, their properness and closure relations for reductive G. The general-G convention (order taken on the reductive quotient M) is new and belongs to route 1.

items.name: Gr_[μ] is cut out by the specialization condition in a faithful representation
items.statement: For every representation ρ: G → GL_n, the restriction of Gr_G → Gr_{GL_n} to Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M} lands in the lattices of type ≥ [ρ∘μ]; if ρ is faithful, Gr_[μ] = (Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M}) ∩ (Gr_G ×_{Gr_{GL_n}} Gr_{≤[ρ∘μ]}). In particular Gr_[μ] is a closed locally spatial subdiamond of Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_{[μ]_M}.

items.name: Neutral p-adic Hodge structures over a diamond
items.statement: Let Y be a locally spatial diamond over Q̆_p. A neutral p-adic Hodge structure on Y is a Q-graded Q_p-vector space V = ⊕_{λ∈Q} V_λ with, for each λ, a B_dR^+-lattice L_λ on V_λ ⊗ B_dR over Y_v such that at every geometric point (V_λ, L_λ) is a p-adic Hodge structure of weight λ (equivalently (V_λ ⊗ O_FF)_{L_λ} is semistable of slope −λ/2 at each geometric point). Example: Q_p(k) = (Q_p, Fil^{-k}B_dR) is the constant Tate structure of weight −2k.

items.name: Neutral p-adic Hodge structures form a neutral Tannakian category
items.statement: The neutral p-adic Hodge structures on Y form a rigid abelian tensor category HS°(Y) over Q_p, neutral Tannakian with fibre functor ω_ét(V, L) = V (as for a point, Part I Theorem 4.3.5).
items.locator: Section 6, paragraph after Example 6.0.2, p. 36 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review note: missing is right. Warning for the design job: the paper gives no proof beyond 'as in the case of a point', and the family version needs an extra argument (new issue 6, a gap). Plan the proof through the pro-étale local triviality of fibrewise-semistable bundles on FF_S.

items.name: Neutral G-p-adic Hodge structures, types and Mumford–Tate groups
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic, a neutral G-p-adic Hodge structure on Y is an exact tensor functor 𝒢: Rep G → HS°(Y) with ω_ét∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std (the isomorphism is not part of the data; with a chosen trivialization it is a p-adic Hodge structure on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system). Its type is the inverse of the type of the associated lattice on the trivial G(B_dR^+)-local system, when that exists. MT(𝒢) = Aut^⊗(ω_ét|_⟨𝒢⟩) is a linear algebraic group over Q_p, a closed subgroup of G after trivialization, and 𝒢 has a canonical MT(𝒢)-structure.
items.locator: Definition 6.1.1, p. 36; Remark 6.1.2 and Section 6.1, p. 36

items.name: The period domain X_[μ]
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group, [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} (so Q_p([μ^{-1}]) = Q_p([μ])), and fix a Levi decomposition G = M ⋉ U. Over Spd Q̆_p([μ]), let L_univ be the universal lattice on the trivial G(B_dR^+)-local system over Gr_{[μ^{-1}],Q̆_p([μ])} := Gr_[μ^{-1}] ×_{Spd Q_p([μ])} Spd Q̆_p([μ]). The modification (E_triv)_{L_univ} (Section 4.3) is then a Gr_{[μ^{-1}],Q̆_p([μ])}-point of Bun_G. If the unique basic element [b] of B(M,[μ^{-1}]) = B(G,[μ^{-1}]) is basic in G (its slope morphism is central in G), define X_[μ] := Gr_{[μ^{-1}],Q̆_p([μ])} ×_{Bun_G} Bun_G^{[b]}, a subdiamond of Gr_{[μ^{-1}],Q̆_p([μ])} over Spd Q̆_p([μ]).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Leaves out the base. The modification (E_triv)_{L_univ} of Section 4.3 needs a base over Spd Q̆_p, and the paper uses X_[μ] over Q̆_p([μ]) throughout: Lemma 6.3.3 takes L/Q̆_p([μ]), and Section 6.4 base-changes to X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}. So X_[μ] is a subdiamond of Gr_[μ^{-1}] ×_{Spd Q_p([μ])} Spd Q̆_p([μ]), not of Gr_[μ^{-1}] over Q_p([μ]). The item should also say G/Q_p is connected linear algebraic.

items.name: X_[μ] is a non-empty open subdiamond of Gr_[μ^{-1}]
items.statement: X_[μ] ⊆ Gr_[μ^{-1}] is a non-empty open subdiamond; moreover X_[μ]/Spd Q̆_p([μ]) admits a rigid analytic point.
items.note: Openness by Theorem 4.2.2; non-emptiness by Part I Example 5.4.6 and Theorem 5.1.6; the rigid point by Proposition 7.3.3 and Theorem 8.5.1.

items.name: X_[μ] is the moduli space of p-adic Hodge structures of type [μ] on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system
items.statement: Let ν be the slope morphism of [b]. The restriction of L_univ on ω_std to X_[μ], with weight grading induced by 2ν, is the universal p-adic Hodge structure of type [μ] and weight 2ν on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system.

items.name: X_[μ] is geometrically connected
items.statement: X_[μ] is geometrically connected.
items.locator: Proposition 6.2.3, p. 37; second assertion; from Theorem 8.5.1 and Proposition 7.3.4

items.name: The Hodge–Tate locus of a line
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be a p-adic Hodge structure on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system over a locally spatial diamond S/Q̆_p, V ∈ Rep G with 𝒢(V) = (V, L), and ℓ ⊆ V_{2n} a line in weight 2n. HT(ℓ) ⊆ S is the subfunctor of f: Y → S with ℓ ⊗_{Q_p} Fil^n B_dR ⊆ f^*L; it is the locus where ℓ underlies a sub-structure (isomorphic to Q_p(−n) = (Q_p, Fil^n B_dR)).

items.name: Hodge–Tate loci are closed
items.statement: HT(ℓ) ⊆ S is a closed subdiamond.
items.locator: Lemma 6.3.2, p. 38; first assertion; by Lemma 2.3.2

items.name: The Hodge–Tate locus is where the Mumford–Tate group stabilizes the line
items.statement: HT(ℓ) is the locus where MT(𝒢|_{HT(ℓ)}) ⊆ Stab_G(ℓ): a map f: T → S with MT(f^*𝒢) ⊆ Stab_G(ℓ) factors through HT(ℓ).

items.name: Hodge–Tate loci on rigid analytic varieties are Zariski closed
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be connected linear algebraic, [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p}, L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field, S/Spa L a seminormal rigid analytic variety, and 𝒢 a p-adic Hodge structure of type [μ] on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system over S^♢. Let V ∈ Rep G with 𝒢(V) = (V, L), and ℓ ⊆ V_{2n} a line. The classifying map S^♢ → Gr_{[μ^{-1}]} (for G_L), composed with BB, is by Theorem 5.0.4(4) (equivalently Proposition 5.0.3(4), since S is seminormal) the diamond of a filtration Fil^• of type [μ] on the trivial G-bundle on S_ét. For each V this is a filtration of V ⊗ O_{S_ét} by local direct summands, and its pullback to V ⊗ O is the trace (Hodge–Tate) filtration of L. Then HT(ℓ) ⊆ S^♢ is rigid analytic: it is the Zariski closed subset of |S| = |S^♢| where a basis vector s of ℓ maps to 0 in (V ⊗ O_{S_ét})/Fil^{-n}. (For S smooth, Fil^• is also the filtration of Theorem 3.3.1(3).)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item gets the Hodge–Tate filtration from Theorem 3.3.1. That theorem (following Scholze's p-adic Hodge theory paper, §7) is stated only for smooth rigid varieties, but S here is only seminormal. The paper's proof has the same flaw (new issue 4), and the lemma is used on singular seminormal Y in the proof of Theorem 9.1.3, p. 57. The filtration must come from Theorem 5.0.4(4) (BB plus Proposition 5.0.3(4)), which holds for seminormal S.

items.name: Functoriality of period domains for subgroups
items.statement: Let H ≤ G be a connected closed subgroup and [μ_H] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of H_{Q̄_p} contained in [μ]. Suppose the unique basic element [b_H] of B(H,[μ_H^{-1}]) = B(M_H,[μ_H^{-1}]) is basic in H, and its image [b_G] in B(G) is basic. Then [b_G] is the basic element of B(G,[μ^{-1}]), and push-out along H ≤ G gives a functoriality map X_[μ_H] → X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}, which is injective because Gr_H → Gr_G is injective (Lemma 5.1.1).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Leaves out that H is connected. X_[μ_H] and Gr_H are defined only for connected linear algebraic groups (Definition 5.0.1, Section 6.2); in the application H is a Mumford–Tate group, which is connected. Also, 'a basic class [b_H] ∈ B(H,[μ_H^{-1}])' means, as in Section 6.2 for H, that the unique basic element of B(M_H,[μ_H^{-1}]) is basic in H.

items.name: Period domains of subgroups are closed when minuscule on the Levi
items.statement: If H = M_H ⋉ U_H is a Levi decomposition and [μ_H] is M_H-minuscule, X_[μ_H] is a closed subdiamond of X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}; in particular this holds if [μ_H] has weights ≥ −1 on Lie H, and then X_[μ_H] is rigid analytic (an open in Fl^♢_[μ_H]).
items.locator: Proposition 6.4.1, p. 39; and the paragraph after it, p. 39

items.name: Special subvarieties of X_[μ]
items.statement: For C/Q̆_p algebraically closed non-archimedean, a special subvariety of X_{[μ],C} is a closed rigid analytic subdiamond of the form X_{[μ_H],C} with [μ_H] of weights ≥ −1 on Lie H.

items.name: Neutral admissible pairs over a diamond
items.statement: For Y/Spd Q̆_p a locally spatial diamond, a neutral admissible pair is (W, L_ét) with W an isocrystal and L_ét a B_dR^+-lattice in W ⊗ B_dR over Y such that every geometric restriction is an admissible pair (equivalently E(W)_{L_ét} on the relative curve is semistable of slope 0); morphisms are isocrystal maps f with f_{B_dR}(L) ⊆ L'. AdmPair°(Y) has tensor products and duals.

items.name: Neutral admissible pairs form a neutral Tannakian category
items.statement: AdmPair°(Y) is a neutral Tannakian category over Q_p with fibre functor ω_y(W, L) = H^0(FF_{C♭}, E(W)_{y^*L}) for any geometric point y: Spd(C, C^+) → Y (images and coimages agree by a slope argument at geometric points; ω_y is faithful because a morphism is determined by its map of isocrystals).

items.name: Realizations of neutral admissible pairs
items.statement: On AdmPair°(Y): the isocrystalline realization ω_Isoc(W, L) = W; the étale realization ω_ét(W, L) = H^0(FF_Y, E(W)_L) in Loc_{Q_p}(Y), an exact tensor functor by the equivalence of slope-zero bundles with Q_p-local systems; the de Rham comparison c_dR: ω_ét ⊗ B_dR ≅ ω_Isoc ⊗ B_dR; the étale lattice ω_{L_ét}(W, L) = L on ω_Isoc ⊗ B_dR; and the de Rham lattice L_dR(W, L) = c_dR^{-1}(W ⊗ B_dR^+) on ω_ét ⊗ B_dR. Example: the Tate pair Q̆_p(n) = ((Q̆_p, p^{-n}φ), Fil^n B_dR).

items.name: Slope-zero bundles on relative curves are Q_p-local systems
items.statement: Vector bundles on the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve that are semistable of slope zero at every geometric point are equivalent to Q_p-local systems (Kedlaya–Liu; Fargues–Scholze, Corollary II.2.20), compatibly with tensor products.
items.locator: Section 7.1, p. 41, the paragraph introducing Eq. (7.1.3.2) (citing Kedlaya–Liu and Fargues–Scholze, Corollary II.2.20) (arXiv v2); p. 39 (Definition 7.1.1) only uses slope-zero semistability, not the equivalence
items.note: Review note: VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals:VB4 plans 'the equivalence between everywhere slope-zero bundles and pro-étale E-local systems, with tensor and scalar-extension compatibility'; that is this item (over a locally spatial diamond Y by v-descent). 'planned' is right.

items.name: Neutral G-admissible pairs and their motivic Galois groups
items.statement: Let Y/Spd Q̆_p be a locally spatial diamond and G/Q_p a connected linear algebraic group. A neutral G-admissible pair on Y is an exact tensor functor 𝒢: Rep G → AdmPair°(Y) such that ω_y∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std for every geometric point y: Spd(C, C^+) → Y. For a geometric point y, MG(𝒢, y) := Aut^⊗(ω_y|⟨𝒢⟩), where ⟨𝒢⟩ is the Tannakian subcategory generated by 𝒢(V) for any faithful V ∈ Rep G; it is a linear algebraic group over Q_p, a trivialization ω_y∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std identifies it with a closed subgroup of G = Aut^⊗(ω_std), and 𝒢 has a canonical refinement to MG(𝒢, y)-structure. [Supplement used implicitly by the paper: MG(𝒢, y) is connected, and when Y is connected the canonical refinement is a neutral MG(𝒢, y)-admissible pair.] A choice of isomorphism ω_Isoc∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std ⊗ Q̆_p (it exists by Steinberg's theorem, Part I §2.2.3) makes ω_{L_ét}∘𝒢 a B_dR^+-lattice on the trivial G(B_dR)-local system, with classifying map Y → Gr_{G,Q̆_p}; another choice changes the map by an element of G(Q̆_p).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Faithful to the paper (with E6's Y in place of the printed S). But the paper never states that MG(𝒢, y) is connected, nor that the canonical refinement is neutral at every geometric point, although Section 7.5 and Lemma 7.5.1 apply constructions defined only for connected H to H = MG(𝒢, y) and call the refinement 'the resulting neutral H-admissible pair'. Connectedness always holds; neutrality holds when Y is connected and can fail otherwise (two new issues). The corrected statement records both.

items.name: The type of a neutral G-admissible pair
items.statement: For Y/Spd Q̆_p([μ]), 𝒢 has type [μ] if the classifying map Y → Gr_{G,Q̆_p([μ])} factors through Gr_[μ] (independent of the trivialization, since Gr_[μ] is G(Q̆_p)-stable). Then the Hodge filtration on (ω_Isoc∘𝒢) ⊗ O has type [μ^{-1}] and the Hodge–Tate filtration on ω_ét ⊗ O (from the de Rham lattice) has type [μ].

items.name: Liu–Zhu rigidity: being de Rham can be checked at one classical point
items.statement: (Liu–Zhu, Invent. Math. 207 (2017), Theorem 3.9(i),(iii),(iv).) Let k be a finite extension of Q_p, X a connected smooth rigid analytic variety over k and 𝕃 a Q_p-local system on X_ét. If the stalk of 𝕃 at one classical point is de Rham, then D_dR(𝕃) = ν_*(𝕃̂ ⊗ OB_dR) is a vector bundle with integrable connection and a filtration by subbundles satisfying Griffiths transversality, and 𝕃 is de Rham in the sense of Scholze (Definition 8.3 there) with this associated filtered flat bundle. (Liu–Zhu Theorem 1.3: for X geometrically connected, not necessarily smooth, the stalks at all classical points are then de Rham with the same Hodge–Tate weights.) The paper uses it over p-adic fields L ⊇ Q̆_p, which needs the (expected) extension of Liu–Zhu's argument to such base fields.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 7.2.3, p. 42, citing [34] = Liu–Zhu, 'Rigidity and a Riemann–Hilbert correspondence for p-adic local systems', Invent. Math. 207 (2017), Theorem 3.9(iv) (arXiv v2)
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6:comparison owns 'the regularity, boundary extension, and arithmetic rigidity statements used by Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu', which is this theorem (the Liu–Zhu extraction also routes it there). Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Two scope points. (a) Liu–Zhu fix k a finite extension of Q_p (Introduction, before their Theorem 1.3; 'k denotes a p-adic field' in their conventions), while the paper applies Theorem 3.9(iv) over p-adic fields L ⊇ Q̆_p; their method (Sen theory over k, Scholze's OB_dR) is expected to extend, but the citation does not literally cover it. (b) Theorem 3.9 is proved in their §3 for smooth X ('So X is a smooth rigid analytic variety over k'), with X connected for (iii)–(iv); the output the paper needs is the filtered flat bundle (D_dR, ∇, Fil), which the item should state. Liu–Zhu's Theorem 1.3 allows singular geometrically connected X (via resolution) but only gives de Rhamness at classical points. Review note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T6:comparison says it owns 'the regularity, boundary extension, and arithmetic rigidity statements used by Diao–Lan–Liu–Zhu'; that covers Liu–Zhu rigidity only implicitly (the stage is about the logarithmic setting). Acceptable as 'planned', but the stage should name Liu–Zhu Theorem 3.9 and its base-field scope explicitly.

items.name: Neutral G-admissible pairs on geometrically connected rigid varieties have a type
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group, L/Q̆_p a p-adic field and S/Spa L a geometrically connected seminormal rigid analytic variety. Then every neutral G-admissible pair 𝒢 on S^♢ has a type: there is a conjugacy class [μ] of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} with Q̆_p([μ]) ⊆ L such that the classifying map S^♢ → Gr_{G,L} factors through Gr_[μ]. (The printed proof covers smooth S; for singular S it is completed on a resolution S̃ → S, whose diamond is a v-cover of S^♢; see source issue E13.)
items.note: Proof: each ω_ét∘𝒢(V) descends to S_ét and is de Rham (Liu–Zhu rigidity and Part I Theorem 5.5.1 at a classical point); its filtered flat bundle is V ⊗ O_{S_ét} with a filtration whose lattice is ω_{L_ét}∘𝒢. The argument as written uses tools for smooth S; see source issue E13. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Faithful to the printed statement, but (i) 'has a type' should be spelled out: Definition 7.2.2 needs S^♢ over Spd Q̆_p([μ]); geometric connectedness makes the type Gal(L̄/L)-stable, so Q̆_p([μ]) ⊆ L; (ii) G must be connected (Definition 7.2.1); (iii) the note should record that E13 is confirmed and that the proof is completed through a resolution of singularities (the smooth-locus alternative alone does not suffice).

items.name: b-rigidifications and the b-admissible locus
items.statement: For b ∈ G(Q̆_p), a b-rigidification of a neutral G-admissible pair 𝒢 is an isomorphism ρ_Isoc: W_b ≅ ω_Isoc∘𝒢, W_b the G-isocrystal V ↦ (V_{Q̆_p}, bφ). Gr_G^{b-adm} ⊆ Gr_{G,Q̆_p} is the preimage of the open substack Bun_G^{[1]} under L ↦ (E_b)_L (the locus where the modification is the trivial G-bundle), and Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} := Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])} ×_{Gr_G} Gr_G^{b-adm}.

items.name: Gr_G^{b-adm} represents b-rigidified admissible pairs
items.statement: Pullback of the universal pair (b, L_univ) induces Gr_G^{b-adm}(S) = {(𝒢, ρ_Isoc): 𝒢 ∈ G-AdmPair°(S), ρ_Isoc: W_b ≅ ω_Isoc∘𝒢}/≅, and Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} parameterizes b-rigidified admissible pairs of type [μ].

items.name: The b-admissible locus is open
items.statement: Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} is open in Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])}.

items.name: Reductive case: non-emptiness of admissible loci
items.statement: For G reductive, Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} ≠ ∅ implies [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) (Caraiani–Scholze, Proposition 3.5.3), and if [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) the admissible locus has a rigid analytic point (Rapoport–Viehmann, Proposition 3.1).
items.note: Review note: No atlas stage plans admissible loci, Caraiani–Scholze Proposition 3.5.3 or Rapoport–Viehmann Proposition 3.1 (searched 'admissible locus', 'Rapoport.Viehmann', 'Caraiani.Scholze', 'weakly admissible', 'period domain'); 'missing' is right, and route 7 (HeckeStacksAndLocalShtukas:HS2, local shtuka moduli) is only a loose source home for it.

items.name: The b-admissible locus is non-empty exactly for [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), and then has a rigid point
items.statement: Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} is non-empty if and only if [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]); when non-empty, Gr_[μ]^{b-adm}/Spd Q̆_p([μ]) admits a rigid analytic point (the printed statement names Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])}; see source issue E7).
items.note: Reduced to the Levi quotient via M → G → M (identity on admissible loci).

items.name: Reductive case: connectedness of admissible loci (Gleason–Lourenço)
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be reductive and [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]). Then the open cell Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ]} and the closed cell Gr^{b-adm}_{≤[μ]} over Spd Q̆_p([μ]) are non-empty with connected geometric fibres (Gleason–Lourenço, arXiv:2210.08625, Theorem 1.1/3.1 and the proof of Theorem 3.2, where the open cell is Gr°_{G,μ} and the closed one Gr_{G,μ}).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Gleason–Lourenço assume b ∈ B(G, μ) in their convention (arXiv:2210.08625, Section 3: 'such that b ∈ B(G, µ)'), i.e. [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) here; for other [b] the locus is empty. The hypothesis should be stated. Their Theorem 1.1/3.1 is for the closed cell Gr_{G,μ}; the open-cell statement is inside the proof of Theorem 3.2, as the paper says. Review note: No atlas stage plans the Gleason–Lourenço connectedness theorem (searched 'Gleason', 'admissible locus', 'period domain'); 'missing' is right.

items.name: Cohomological smoothness of Schubert cells and truncated positive loop groups
items.statement: (1) Over an algebraically closed C/Q̆_p([μ_M]), the open Schubert cell Gr_{[μ_M],C} of a reductive group M is connected and ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spd C (ℓ ≠ p, Fargues–Scholze Proposition VI.2.4), hence so (smoothness only) is its open subdiamond Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_M],C}. (2) For a unipotent group U over Q_p and m ≥ 1, U(B_dR^+/Fil^m B_dR^+) is a connected locally spatial diamond, ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spd C: filtering U by a central series with vector-group quotients and B_dR^+/Fil^m by the Fil^j/Fil^{j+1} ≅ O, it is an iterated torsor under vector groups (A^1_C)^{♢,d}.
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness plans truncated positive loop groups and the ℓ-cohomological smoothness of open cells. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The paper (p. 44) asserts 'Each of U(B_dR^+/Fil^m B_dR^+) and Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_M],C} is connected and cohomologically smooth over Spd C' without citation; the Fargues–Scholze numbers are the extraction's. FS VI.2.4 concerns open Schubert cells of reductive groups and does not cover U(B_dR^+/Fil^m) for the unipotent radical U of a non-reductive group, which needs its own (easy) argument; also only ℓ-cohomological smoothness, not connectedness, passes to the open subset Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_M],C}. Review note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS0:Schubert-smoothness plans part (1) (truncated positive loop groups of reductive G and FS VI.2.4/IV.1.18). Part (2), U(B_dR^+/Fil^m) for an arbitrary unipotent U, is not literally planned there: add a request to GS0 or give it to route 1.

items.name: The b-admissible locus is geometrically connected
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group and [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]). Then Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ]}/Spd Q̆_p([μ]) is non-empty and geometrically connected. (For G = MU with b ∈ M(Q̆_p): U(B_dR^+) preserves Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ]} since Bun_G^{[1]} = Bun_M^{[1]} ×_{Bun_M} Bun_G; its action on Gr_[μ] factors through U(B_dR^+/Fil^m) once m exceeds the weights of μ on Lie U; and U(B_dR^+/Fil^m) ×_{Spd C} Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_M],C} → Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ],C} is surjective on underlying spaces, so the reductive case and Lemma 7.3.5 give the result.)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Proposition 7.3.4 (and the item) omit non-emptiness: the locus is empty unless [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]) (Proposition 7.3.3), and 'connected' in the proof (Lemma 7.3.5, counting π_0) means non-empty and connected. State the hypothesis.

items.name: Six-functor identities and the Künneth formula for diamonds
items.statement: For f: X → Y cohomologically smooth, Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible, Rf^!(K) = Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗ f^*K and exceptional pullback composes (ECD Proposition 23.12(i),(iii)); Rf_! satisfies the Künneth formula for fibre products over Spd C (Hansen, Proposition 4.2).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 7.3.5, p. 45 (arXiv v2), citing [39] = Scholze, Étale cohomology of diamonds, Proposition 23.12(i),(iii), and [20] = Hansen, Proposition 4.2 and the proof of Corollary 4.11
items.note: The Künneth formula for Rf_! follows from base change (ECD 22.19) and the projection formula (22.23), planned in S2; 23.12 is planned in S4. Review note: DiamondSixOperations S4 plans ECD 23.10–23.12 (dualizing object, base change of the dualizing object), S3 the composition law for Rf^!, and S2 base change 22.19 and the projection formula 22.23, from which the Künneth formula follows. 'planned' is right.

items.name: Products of connected cohomologically smooth diamonds are connected
items.statement: Let C be an algebraically closed non-archimedean extension of Q_p, ℓ ≠ p a prime, and X, Y non-empty connected locally spatial diamonds that are ℓ-cohomologically smooth over Spd C. Then X ×_{Spd C} Y is connected. (For f: S → Spd C cohomologically smooth with S non-empty, S is connected iff R^0f_!Rf^!F_ℓ ≅ F_ℓ.)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: ℓ-cohomological smoothness is only defined for ℓ ≠ p, and the criterion 'connected iff R^0f_!Rf^!F_ℓ = F_ℓ' presupposes S non-empty; say so.

items.name: The Hodge locus of a rank-one sub-isocrystal
items.statement: Let 𝒢 = (W_b, L) be a b-rigidified G-admissible pair on S/Q̆_p, V ∈ Rep G and ℓ ⊆ V_{Q̆_p} underlying a sub-isocrystal ℓ ≅ Q̆_p(n) = (Q̆_p, p^{-n}φ) of W_b(V). Hdg(ℓ)(Y) = {f: Y → S : ℓ ⊗ Fil^n B_dR ⊆ f^*L(V)} (inside V ⊗ B_dR(Y)), the locus where ℓ underlies a sub-admissible pair; equivalently where (ℓ, (ℓ ⊗ B_dR) ∩ f^*L(V)) is in AdmPair°(Y).

items.name: Hodge loci do not depend on the representative of [b]
items.statement: If b' = gbσ(g)^{-1} with g ∈ G(Q̆_p), the isomorphism Gr_G^{b-adm} ≅ Gr_G^{b'-adm}, L ↦ gL, restricts to Hdg(ℓ) ≅ Hdg(g·ℓ).

items.name: Hodge loci are closed
items.statement: Hdg(ℓ) ⊆ S is a closed subdiamond.

items.name: Hodge loci on rigid analytic varieties are Zariski closed
items.statement: Let L/Q̆_p([μ]) be a p-adic field, S/Spa L seminormal rigid analytic and 𝒢 a b-rigidified admissible pair of type [μ] on S^♢. Then Hdg(ℓ) ⊆ S^♢ is rigid analytic, i.e. corresponds to a Zariski closed subset of S.
items.note: Review note: 'missing' is right. Proof note for the blueprint: the printed proof (by reference to Lemma 6.3.3) takes the filtration from Theorem 3.3.1, which is stated for smooth S only; for seminormal S take it from Proposition 5.0.3(4)/Theorem 5.0.4(4) instead (new issue).

items.name: Functoriality maps between admissible loci
items.statement: For f: H → G a homomorphism of connected linear algebraic groups, b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p), b_G ∈ G(Q̆_p) and g ∈ G(Q̆_p) with g f(b_H) σ(g^{-1}) = b_G, push-out composed with the Hecke action of g gives Gr_H^{b_H-adm} → Gr_G^{b_G-adm}, L ↦ g·(L ×^H G), whose value at V ∈ Rep G is the lattice g L(f^*V).

items.name: Reduction to the motivic Galois group factors the classifying map
items.statement: Let Y/Spd Q̆_p be a connected locally spatial diamond, 𝒢 the neutral G-admissible pair induced by f: Y → Gr_G^{b-adm}, y a geometric point, and fix ω_y∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std, identifying H := MG(𝒢, y) (a connected group) with a closed subgroup of G; let ℋ be the canonical reduction of 𝒢 to H (a neutral H-admissible pair because Y is connected). (1) There are b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p) with image [b] in B(G) and g ∈ G(Q̆_p) with g b_H σ(g)^{-1} = b such that f factors as the functoriality map Gr_H^{b_H-adm} → Gr_G^{b-adm} composed with a map f': Y → Gr_H^{b_H-adm}, and f'^* of the universal neutral H-admissible pair is ℋ. (For disconnected Y, apply this on each connected component.)
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.1, pp. 46–47 (statement begins on p. 46; parts (1) and (2) are on p. 47) (arXiv v2)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: As printed, and in the item, Y is an arbitrary locally spatial diamond. Then the canonical reduction ℋ of 𝒢 to H = MG(𝒢, y) need not be a neutral H-admissible pair and the lemma fails (counterexample with Y = Spd C ⊔ Spd C in the new issue); it holds for connected Y, which is all the paper uses. H = MG(𝒢, y) must also be known to be connected (new gap issue). Locator: parts (1) and (2) are on p. 47.

items.name: Over a geometrically connected rigid base the reduction lands in one Schubert cell
items.statement: If moreover Y is a geometrically connected rigid analytic diamond over a p-adic field Spd L (so L ⊇ Q̆_p), then 𝒢 has a type [μ] with Q̆_p([μ]) ⊆ L (Theorem 7.2.3), and any f' as in Lemma 7.5.1(1) factors through an open Schubert cell Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} for a conjugacy class [μ_H] of cocharacters of H_{Q̄_p} contained in [μ] with Q̆_p([μ_H]) ⊆ L (Theorem 7.2.3 applied to ℋ).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: [μ] is not defined in Lemma 7.5.1 (new misprint issue): it is the type of 𝒢, which exists by Theorem 7.2.3; the cell Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} also needs Q̆_p([μ_H]) ⊆ L, and Theorem 7.2.3 applies to ℋ only because H is connected and ℋ neutral (Y is connected).

items.name: Admissible loci of closed subgroups are closed subdiamonds
items.statement: Let H ≤ G be a closed connected subgroup, b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p), b_G ∈ G(Q̆_p) and g ∈ G(Q̆_p) with g b_H σ(g)^{-1} = b_G. Then the functoriality map identifies Gr_H^{b_H-adm} with a closed subdiamond of Gr_G^{b_G-adm}. More precisely, for g = 1 and H = Stab_G(ℓ) for a line ℓ in some W ∈ Rep G (ℓ_Q̆p a sub-isocrystal via b_H), Gr_H^{b_H-adm} is an open and closed subdiamond of the Hodge locus Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p) (closed by Lemma 7.4.3), equal to it when ker(H^1(Q_p, H) → H^1(Q_p, G)) is trivial. The map Gr_{H,Q̆p} → Gr_{G,Q̆p} is injective but need not be closed for non-reductive H: for G = GL_2, H the upper-triangular Borel, g = 1 and b_H = b_G = diag(1, p), over the Schubert cell of μ = diag(t^{-1}, 1) the map on Grassmannians restricted to the B-cell of type diag(1, t^{-1}) is the open inclusion A^1 → P^1, while on admissible loci it is an isomorphism A^1 ≅ A^1.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Two corrections, both new issues. (a) The item says Gr_H^{b_H-adm} is 'namely the Hodge locus Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p)'; the proof's identification fails when ker(H^1(Q_p, H) → H^1(Q_p, G)) ≠ 1 (e.g. G = SL_2, H an anisotropic torus, b = 1): Gr_H^{b_H-adm} is only an open and closed part of Hdg(ℓ). The proposition itself (closedness) is true. (b) The Borel example of Remark 7.5.3 is miscomputed with b = diag(p, 1): the b_H-admissible locus over that Schubert cell is one point; the described picture holds with b_H = b_G = diag(1, p).

items.name: Special subdiamonds of admissible loci
items.statement: A special subdiamond of Gr_G^{b_G-adm} is a closed subdiamond identified with some Gr_H^{b_H-adm} by a functoriality map.

items.name: Schubert cells with weights at most one in admissible loci are closed rigid analytic
items.statement: Suppose the weights of [μ_H] on Lie H are ≤ 1 and [b_H] ∈ B(H, [μ_H^{-1}]). Then Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} is a non-empty geometrically connected rigid analytic diamond over Q̆_p([μ_H]) (an open subdiamond of Gr_{[μ_H]} = Fl^♢_{[μ_H^{-1}]}), closed in Gr^{b_H-adm}_{H,Q̆_p([μ_H])}. Via the functoriality map it is a closed geometrically connected rigid analytic subdiamond of Gr^{b_G-adm}_{G,Q̆_p([μ_H])}, contained in Gr^{b_G-adm}_{[μ_G],Q̆_p([μ_H])}, [μ_G] the induced class.
items.locator: Lemma 7.5.5, p. 48; and the paragraph after it, p. 48
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Add [b_H] ∈ B(H, [μ_H^{-1}]): otherwise Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} is empty (Proposition 7.3.3) and the cited Proposition 7.3.4 gives nothing. (The following paragraph also writes Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ_G],…} for Gr^{b_G-adm}_{[μ_G],…}.)

items.name: Special subvarieties of admissible loci
items.statement: For C/Q̆_p algebraically closed, a special subvariety of Gr^{b_G-adm}_{G,C} or Gr^{b_G-adm}_{[μ_G],C} is a closed connected rigid analytic subdiamond identified with some Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H],C} for [μ_H] with weights ≤ 1 on Lie H; those from tori are special points.

items.name: The Kottwitz map for tori
items.statement: For a torus T, Kottwitz's map κ_T: B(T) → X_*(T)_{Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p)} is an isomorphism, and B(T, [μ]) is the single class b_μ with κ_T([b_μ]) = μ^#.
items.note: Review note: BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 plans the Kottwitz map κ, its relation to ν 'for tori and GL_n' and the classification assertions for B(G); κ_T: B(T) ≅ X_*(T)_Γ and B(T, [μ]) = {b_μ} fall under it. 'planned' is right.

items.name: Admissible loci of tori
items.statement: For a torus T over Q_p and μ ∈ X_*(T): Gr_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ])} = Gr^{b_{μ^{-1}}-adm}_{[μ]} ≅ Spd Q̆_p([μ]) (a single point). For b ∈ T(Q̆_p), Gr_T^{b-adm} is the disjoint union, over the Gal(Q̄_p/Q̆_p)-orbits of those μ ∈ X_*(T) with μ^# = κ_T([b]), of the images of Gr_{[μ^{-1}]} ≅ Spd Q̆_p([μ]); after base change to an algebraically closed C, Gr^{b-adm}_{T,C} = ⊔_{μ^# = κ_T([b])} Spd C.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Printed as 'Gr_[μ] = Gr^{b_{μ^{-1}}-adm}_{[μ]} ≅ Spd Q_p([μ])' and a disjoint union over all μ with μ^# = κ_T([b]). The admissible locus lives over Q̆_p([μ]) (Section 7.3), and when T is ramified, inertia-conjugate μ give the same point of Gr_{T,Q̆_p}, so the union must run over Gal(Q̄_p/Q̆_p)-orbits (or be read after base change to C). New misprint issue.

items.name: Special subvarieties move in G_b(Q_p)-families; the Lubin–Tate example
items.statement: The special subvarieties attached to (H, [μ_H]) depend only on its G(Q_p)-conjugacy class but vary with the element g σ-conjugating b_H to b_G, i.e. under G_b(Q_p). In the height-two Lubin–Tate case (admissible locus P^1_{Q̆_p}) with H = F^×, F/Q_p quadratic, the special points (formal groups with endomorphisms by F) form one G_b(Q_p)-orbit identified with P^1(F), G_b(Q_p) the units of the quaternion division algebra.

items.name: Intersections of admissible loci with Schubert cells
items.statement: If H is reductive, the classes [μ_H] refining [μ] are incomparable in the Bruhat order and (after a finite extension) Gr^{b_H-adm}_{H,Q̆_p([μ])} ∩ Gr_[μ]^{b_G-adm} = ⊔_{[μ_H]⊆[μ]} Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]}; the special subvarieties of Gr_[μ]^{b_G-adm} are the rigid analytic connected components of such intersections. For non-reductive H, Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} need not be closed in Gr_H^{b_H-adm} ∩ Gr_[μ_G]^{b_G-adm}.

items.name: A non-closed special cell inside a Schubert cell
items.statement: Let G = GL_3, H the parabolic stabilizing ⟨e_1, e_2⟩ with Levi GL_2 × GL_1, and on D_C = Spa C⟨z⟩ let L_z = ⟨e_1, e_2 + (z/ξ)e_1, e_3 + (1/ξ)e_1⟩ = ⟨ξe_3, e_2 − ze_3, (1/ξ)(ξe_3 + e_1)⟩. Then (Q̆_p^3, L_z) is a neutral admissible pair (b = 1), L_z ∈ Gr_[μ] for μ = (t, 1, t^{-1}), L_z ∈ Gr_H^{1-adm}, for z ≠ 0 L_z ∈ Gr^{1-adm}_{[μ_H],H} with μ_H = (t, t^{-1}) × 1, but L_0 ∉ Gr_{[μ_H],H}; so Gr^{1-adm}_{[μ_H]} is not closed in Gr_H^{1-adm} ∩ Gr_[μ]^{1-adm}.

items.name: The infinite-level moduli space M_b
items.statement: For G/Q_p connected linear algebraic and b ∈ G(Q̆_p), M_b/Spd Q̆_p classifies (𝒢, ρ_Isoc, ρ_ét) with 𝒢 a neutral G-admissible pair, ρ_Isoc: W_b ≅ ω_Isoc∘𝒢 and ρ_ét: ω_std ⊗ Q_p ≅ ω_ét∘𝒢. The forgetful map π_{L_ét}: M_b → Gr_G^{b-adm} is the G(Q_p)-torsor Isom(ω_std ⊗ Q_p, ω_ét∘𝒢), so M_b is a locally spatial diamond; M_{b,[μ]} := M_b ×_{Gr_G^{b-adm}} Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} is a locally closed subdiamond of M_{b,Q̆_p([μ])}.
items.note: Review note: Matches p. 50. The printed fibre product is over Gr^{b-adm}_{G,Q̆_p}.

items.name: M_b is the moduli of modifications from E_b to the trivial bundle
items.statement: A modification α: E_b ⇢ E_triv (an isomorphism off ∞ with locally bounded poles) gives the lattice π_{L_ét}(α) = α_{B_dR}^{-1}(E_triv|_{B_dR^+}) ⊆ W_b ⊗ B_dR and a b-rigidified admissible pair with canonical étale and isocrystalline trivializations; this identifies M_b(S) with the set of modifications E_b ⇢ E_triv over S.

items.name: The period maps of M_{b,[μ]}
items.statement: π_{L_ét}(𝒢, ρ_ét, ρ_Isoc) = ρ_Isoc^*((ω_ét∘𝒢) ⊗ B_dR^+) and π_{L_dR}(𝒢, ρ_ét, ρ_Isoc) = ρ_ét^*((ω_Isoc∘𝒢) ⊗ B_dR^+), lattices on ω_std ⊗ B_dR, give M_b → Gr_G (twice); on M_{b,[μ]} they land in Gr_[μ] and Gr_[μ^{-1}], and composing with BB gives the Hodge and Hodge–Tate period maps π_Hdg: M_{b,[μ]} → Fl_[μ^{-1}] and π_HT: M_{b,[μ]} → Fl_[μ]. For b basic, ρ_ét^*L_dR is a p-adic Hodge structure on the trivial G(Q_p)-local system and π_{L_dR} factors through X_[μ].

items.name: For b basic, π_{L_dR} is a G_b(Q_p)-torsor over X_[μ]
items.statement: For b basic, π_{L_dR}: M_{b,[μ]} → X_[μ] is a G_b(Q_p)-torsor; in particular the G_b(Q_p)-action by change of ρ_Isoc extends to an action of the topological constant sheaf G_b(Q_p) (clear from the modification description).

items.name: Functoriality maps of infinite-level moduli spaces
items.statement: For ι: H ↪ G closed connected, [μ_H] ⊆ [μ], b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p) representing the basic class of B(H, [μ_H^{-1}]) and g ∈ G(Q̆_p) with g^{-1}bσ(g) = b_H, push-out and g: E_{ι(b_H)} ≅ E_b give M_{b_H,[μ_H]} → M_{b,[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}, Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H]} → Gr^{b-adm}_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])} and, for b basic, X_[μ_H] → X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}, compatibly with group actions and period maps.
items.note: Review note: The statement already applies E8 (g ∈ G(Q̆_p)) and E9 (X_{[μ],Q̆_p([μ_H])}). The relation should read g^{-1}bσ(g) = ι(b_H). b is basic throughout §8.4, so the paper's 'if b is basic' is redundant.

items.name: Hodge and Hodge–Tate special subvarieties at infinite level
items.statement: Let [μ] admit a basic class [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field, C = L̄^, M = M_{b,[μ]}. (1) A Hodge special subvariety of M_C is a connected component of a closed subdiamond M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} with [μ_H] of weights ≤ 1 on Lie H; equivalently a connected component of the π_{L_ét}-preimage of a special subvariety Gr^{b_H-adm}_{[μ_H],C}. (2) For b basic, a Hodge–Tate special subvariety is a connected component of such an M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} with weights ≥ −1 on Lie H; equivalently of the π_{L_dR}-preimage of a special subvariety X_{[μ_H],C} of X_{[μ],C}.
items.note: Review note: Statement matches. In §8.4, b represents the basic class by assumption, so the 'if b is basic' in (2) and in Lemma 8.4.2 is redundant, though harmless (Remark 9.1.4 applies (1) and (3) to non-basic b).

items.name: Special subvarieties at infinite level
items.statement: A special subvariety of M_C is a connected component of a closed subdiamond M_{b_H,[μ_H],C} with [μ_H] minuscule on Lie H (weights in [−1, 1]).

items.name: Special means both Hodge special and Hodge–Tate special
items.statement: If b is basic, a closed connected subdiamond of M_C is a special subvariety if and only if it is both a Hodge special and a Hodge–Tate special subvariety (take H the motivic Galois group, equivalently the Mumford–Tate group, of the universal pair restricted to it).

items.name: When the three notions of special subvariety agree
items.statement: If [μ] is minuscule, Hodge special subvarieties and special subvarieties coincide, and for b basic they are also the Hodge–Tate special subvarieties, with no weight condition needed; the three notions also agree when H is reductive.

items.name: A Hodge special subvariety that is not Hodge–Tate special
items.statement: Let E/Q_p be a cubic extension, G = Res_{E/Q_p} GL_2 and H ≤ G the mirabolic subgroup (* *; 0 1) = E^× ⋉ E. With E^×_{Q̄_p} = G_m^3 and μ_H = μ: t ↦ (t, t, t^{-2}), the basic elements are b_H = b = 1, and the associated Hodge special subvariety is not Hodge–Tate special (the weights of μ_H on Lie H are 0, 1, 1, −2).
items.note: Review note: Checked. The weights of μ_H = (1, 1, −2) on Lie H = Lie E^× ⊕ E are 0 (multiplicity 3), 1, 1 and −2, so they are ≤ 1 but not ≥ −1. μ is not minuscule for G = (GL_2)^3 over Q̄_p (weights ±1, ±2). b = 1 is basic in G and in H: κ(μ^{-1}) = 0 in π_1(G)_Γ ≅ Z and in X_*(E^×)_Γ ≅ Z.

items.name: Basic duality: M_b ≅ M_{b^{-1}} for the inner form G_b
items.statement: Let b ∈ G(Q̆_p) be basic. Then b_{G_b}^{-1} is basic in G_b(Q̆_p), and twisting by F_b (a modification E_triv ⇢ E_b becomes E_{b^{-1}_{G_b}} ⇢ E_triv via Lemma 4.2.3) is a G(Q_p) × G_b(Q_p)-equivariant isomorphism M_b ≅ M_{b^{-1}_{G_b}} exchanging the de Rham and étale lattice period maps.
items.note: For GL_n and the Lubin–Tate/Drinfeld towers this is the Faltings–Fargues isomorphism planned in EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6a; the PEL normalization differs by a transpose (Remark 8.5.2). Review note: The note's planned-stage claim holds: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6a plans the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers and 'the infinite-level moduli description and duality isomorphism' for GL_n by the Scholze–Weinstein route. The general non-reductive statement stays missing (route 1).

items.name: Basic duality exchanges the Hodge and Hodge–Tate structures
items.statement: For each [μ] such that [b] is the basic element of B(G, [μ^{-1}]), the duality restricts to M_{b,[μ]} ≅ M_{b^{-1}_{G_b},[μ^{-1}]}, exchanging the Hodge and Hodge–Tate period maps and the Hodge and Hodge–Tate special subvarieties.

items.name: Hodge and Hodge–Tate analytic Zariski closures, irreducible analytic sets and bi-analytic sets
items.statement: Let M = M_{b,[μ]} with [b] basic in B(G, [μ^{-1}]), L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field, C = L̄^, 𝔍 = Gal(L̄/L). For A ⊂ |M_C| the Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic Zariski closure is the intersection of all preimages of closed rigid analytic subdiamonds (over C^K) of M_C/K containing A, K ≤ G(Q_p) × 𝔍 (resp. K ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍) compact open. An irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set is a connected component of the preimage of an irreducible locally closed rigid analytic subdiamond of some M_C/K; a locally closed subdiamond is bi-analytic if it is both. (In the minuscule case these closures are the closures for the limit Zariski topologies; in general it is unclear whether finite unions of closed rigid analytic subdiamonds are rigid analytic.)

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3(1): special subvarieties are Zariski closed irreducible analytic sets
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected linear algebraic group, [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p} admitting a basic class [b] ∈ B(G, [μ^{-1}]), b ∈ G(Q̆_p) representing [b], and M = M_{b,[μ]}. Let L/Q̆_p([μ]) be a p-adic field, C = L̄^ and 𝔍 = Gal(L̄/L), with closures and analytic sets as in Definition 9.1.1 for this 𝔍. Then Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) special subvarieties of M_C (Definition 8.4.1) are Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytically Zariski closed irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic sets in M_C.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item leaves out the field data that Theorem 9.1.3 inherits from the preamble of §9.1 (p. 55). M_C and every closure and analytic set depend on L through C = L̄^ and 𝔍 = Gal(L̄/L). L is only a p-adic field over Q̆_p([μ]) (perfect residue field, not necessarily strict).

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3(2): the bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 9.1.3, the Hodge–Tate (resp. Hodge) analytic Zariski closure of an irreducible Hodge (resp. Hodge–Tate) analytic set is a Hodge–Tate (resp. Hodge) special subvariety, unless the defining intersection is indexed by the empty set (in which case it is all of M_C).
items.note: Review note: Setting as corrected in item 155 (L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field). The proof on pp. 56–58 has three gaps that are easy to repair (see the new issues): it applies Lemma 9.3.1 to a Z known only to be irreducible and geometrically connected; it applies Part I Corollary 5.5.3, which is stated for strict fields, at a classical point over a field that need not be strict; and K'_b is misprinted (E11).

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3: the closed bi-analytic sets are the special subvarieties
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 9.1.3, special subvarieties are the only closed bi-analytic sets in M_C.
items.note: Review note: Checked. A closed bi-analytic Y has its own image as a closed rigid analytic subdiamond at every finite level, so it equals both its Hodge and its Hodge–Tate closure. Part (2) then makes it Hodge special and Hodge–Tate special, and Lemma 8.4.2 makes it special. Special subvarieties are bi-analytic and closed by part (1).

items.name: Without the basic hypothesis special subvarieties need not be Hodge–Tate closed
items.statement: For the generic fibre of the Serre–Tate deformation space of μ_{p^∞} × Q_p/Z_p (G the upper-triangular group, μ = diag(z^{-1}, 1), b = diag(p, 1)), the Hodge–Tate period map has one-point image, so the special point of the canonical lift (the diagonal torus) cannot be cut out by conditions on the Hodge–Tate filtration.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate period map is a submersion at a Hodge-generic classical point
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem 9.1.3(2), after reducing to G = H the motivic Galois group: let Y be a connected closed rigid analytic subdiamond of M_C/K_b containing the image of Z̃, z ∈ Z(C) a Hodge-generic classical point with image y. Then an open subgroup of 𝔍 moves y through an orbit K_0·y of a compact open K_0 ≤ G(Q_p) (Part I Corollary 5.5.3 and Lemma 9.3.3); for a smooth locally closed V ⊆ Y containing K_0·y on which df has constant rank k, with f: V → Fl_{[μ],E} induced by BB∘π_{L_dR}, one has k = dim Fl_[μ] (a function vanishing on the orbit K_0·f(y) of the submersive orbit map vanishes near f(y)). Hence df_y is surjective, Griffiths transversality forces the weights of [μ] on Lie G to be ≥ −1, M_C/K_b is étale over Fl^♢_{[μ],E}, and dimension count gives that Y is the connected component of M_C/K_b through y.
items.locator: Section 9.2, p. 56; proof of Theorem 9.1.3, pp. 57–58
items.note: Review note: Faithful summary of pp. 57–58. Three corrections apply: (i) the reduction to H uses K'_b = (g H_{b_H}(Q_p) g^{-1} × 𝔍) ∩ K_b (E11). (ii) The Galois-orbit step needs Part I Corollary 5.5.3, which Part I states only for strict fields. When L is not strict, apply it over the completed maximal unramified extension F' of the field of definition F of z: ρ(Gal(C/F')) is open in MG = G(Q_p), and the orbit of y under an open subgroup of Gal(C/F) contains K_0·y, which is all the argument needs (new issue). (iii) z comes from Lemma 9.3.1 in the form for irreducible Z (new issue; item 160). The rest (constant rank, the identity theorem on K_0 ⊆ G(C), Griffiths transversality forcing weights ≥ −1, dimension count) checked.

items.name: Lemma 9.3.1: Hodge-generic classical points are dense
items.statement: Let L/Q̆_p be a p-adic field, Z/Spa L an irreducible rigid analytic variety and 𝒢 a neutral G-admissible pair over Z^♢. Then the Hodge generic locus of 𝒢 in |Z| = |Z^♢| contains a dense set of classical points. Proof: take a desingularization S → Z, which is connected because Z is irreducible. If the pair has no type on S (S need not be geometrically connected), work over the field of constants L_S of S, which is finite over L and over which S is geometrically connected; Theorem 7.2.3 then gives a type defined over L_S, so Lemma 7.4.4 applies. Apply Lemma 9.3.5 and push the dense Hodge-generic classical points forward along the proper surjection S → Z. On Z ⊆ M_{b,[μ]}/K the type [μ] is already given.
items.locator: Lemma 9.3.1, p. 58; deduced from Lemma 9.3.5 on a desingularization of Z
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Faithful to p. 58, but the proof of Theorem 9.1.3 (p. 57) applies it to a Z known only to be irreducible and geometrically connected (p. 56). That does not imply geometrically irreducible: {x² = ϖy²} in the unit bidisc over E, with ϖ a non-square, is irreducible and geometrically connected but splits into two lines over E(√ϖ). The lemma holds in the weaker form, and that is the form the roadmap needs (see new issue).

items.name: The Hodge exceptional and Hodge generic loci
items.statement: For a neutral admissible pair 𝒢 on a locally spatial diamond S over Spd Q̆_p, the Hodge exceptional locus is the union of all strictly contained Hodge loci |Hdg(ℓ)| ⊊ |S|, ℓ running over rank-one sub-isocrystals of ω_Isoc(V) for all V ∈ Rep G; the Hodge generic locus is its complement (which may be empty in general).

items.name: Meeting the Hodge generic locus means having the full motivic Galois group
items.statement: Let 𝒢 be a neutral G-admissible pair on a locally spatial diamond S over Spd Q̆_p, T ⊆ S a subdiamond and y a geometric point of T. Then MG(𝒢|_T, y) = MG(𝒢, y) if and only if T is contained in no proper Hodge locus Hdg(ℓ) ⊊ S (ℓ a rank-one sub-isocrystal of ω_Isoc∘𝒢(V), V ∈ Rep G). In particular, if T meets the Hodge generic locus then MG(𝒢|_T, y) = MG(𝒢, y). When T is a single (geometric) point the converse also holds: the point is Hodge generic iff its motivic Galois group is MG(𝒢, y). Only this point case, and the forward direction, are used (Proposition 9.3.4; proof of Theorem 9.1.3, p. 57).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Copies Lemma 9.3.3, whose 'if' direction is false for T that is not a single point (new issue). The proof shows MG(𝒢|_T) ≠ MG(𝒢) iff T lies in one proper Hodge locus Hdg(ℓ) ⊊ S. The Hodge exceptional locus, however, is the union of all such loci.

items.name: The Hodge exceptional locus is a countable union of closed subsets
items.statement: Let S be a locally spatial diamond over Spd Q̆_p and 𝒢 a b-rigidified neutral G-admissible pair on S. The Hodge exceptional locus of 𝒢 is a countable union of closed subsets of |S|. (For V ∈ Rep G and V_k = W_b(V)^{φ=p^{-k}}, the incidence subdiamond I_{V_k} ⊆ P_{V_k}(Q_p) × S of pairs (ℓ, s) with s ∈ Hdg(ℓ) is closed; the lines with Hdg(ℓ) ≠ S form an open set, a countable union of compact opens K_i, and the images of |I_{K_i}| under the proper projection are closed.)
items.note: Review note: Matches pp. 59–60. The proof uses two topological facts that no item records: |P × S| = P × |S| for a profinite set P, and properness of the projection P × S → S. See coverage.

items.name: Baire category theorem
items.statement: A completely (pseudo)metrizable space, such as D_n(L') ≅ O_{L'}^n, is a Baire space: a countable union of closed subsets with empty interior has empty interior.
items.note: Mathlib/Topology/Baire/CompleteMetrizable.lean:26 and Mathlib/Topology/Baire/Lemmas.lean:257. Review note: Verified at Mathlib 082e2d3: BaireSpace.of_completelyPseudoMetrizable (Mathlib/Topology/Baire/CompleteMetrizable.lean:26) and nonempty_interior_of_iUnion_of_closed (Mathlib/Topology/Baire/Lemmas.lean:257; the covering form, with union = univ). The form used on p. 60 (a countable union of closed sets with empty interior has empty interior, i.e. the complement is dense) is dense_iInter_of_isOpen (Mathlib/Topology/Baire/Lemmas.lean:142) after taking complements. Cite it as well.

items.name: On a smooth connected base the Hodge generic locus contains all weakly Shilov points and dense classical points
items.statement: Suppose S is a smooth connected rigid analytic variety over a p-adic field L ⊇ Q̆_p and 𝒢 = (W_b, L) a b-rigidified neutral G-admissible pair on S^♢. Then the Hodge generic locus of 𝒢 is dense in |S| = |S^♢|: it contains all weakly Shilov points (Bhatt–Hansen, Definition 2.5) and a dense set of classical points.
items.note: Proof: a proper Hodge locus is Zariski closed (Lemma 7.4.4) and nowhere dense (Conrad), so contains no weakly Shilov point (Bhatt–Hansen); for classical points, apply the Baire category theorem on L'-disks, using that a closed set containing the L'-points of a disk contains its Gauss point (the residue field is algebraically closed). Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The citation for weakly Shilov points should be Bhatt–Hansen Definition 2.5, not 2.4 (the paper's own misprint; see the new issue). The statement is true as printed, but its proof applies Lemma 7.4.4, which needs a type [μ] over a field containing Q̆_p([μ]). Theorem 7.2.3 supplies a type only on geometrically connected S, and here S is only connected; pass to the field of constants of S.

items.name: Variations of p-adic Hodge structure
items.statement: For S smooth rigid analytic over a p-adic field L, a de Rham local system 𝕃 carries a second lattice M_0 ⊆ 𝕃 ⊗ B_dR from the trivial filtration of its flat bundle. A variation of p-adic Hodge structure over S is a Q-graded de Rham local system 𝕃 = ⊕_λ 𝕃_λ such that each (𝕃_λ, M_{0,λ}) restricts at every geometric point to a p-adic Hodge structure of weight λ. A variation with G-structure is an exact tensor functor from Rep G to variations. (These are neutral only for 𝕃 trivial in weight 0.)

items.name: de Rham torsors and the attached period data
items.statement: Let K ≤ G(Q_p) be open and S̃/S a pro-étale K-torsor that is de Rham (its push-out V ↦ S̃ ×^K V is de Rham, equivalently for one faithful V). The G(Q_p)-local system is a map E_S̃: S^♢ → Bun_G^{[1]}, and modifying by M_0 gives E_S̃^dR: S^♢ → Bun_G. If E_S̃^dR factors through Bun_G^{[b]} with b basic, pulling back the universal G_b(Q_p)-torsor gives S̃^cris/S carrying a neutralized good b-admissible pair with G-structure, an étale lattice period map S̃^cris → Gr_[μ]^{b-adm} for the Hodge cocharacter [μ], and a lift S̃^cris → M_{b,[μ]}/K. (That this gives a variation of p-adic Hodge structure with G-structure is announced for Part III.)

items.name: The Katz–Igusa tower is not refined by a rigid analytic cover
items.statement: For S the ordinary locus of a connected finite-level p-adic modular curve with no level at p and S̃ the Katz–Igusa tower (the Z_p^×-local system trivializing the canonical subgroup), S̃^cris = S̃; it is the generic fibre of a tower of formal schemes but not a rigid analytic space, and since the Katz–Igusa tower is connected the cover cannot be reduced to a rigid analytic variety.

items.name: Bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann on basic loci of Hodge-type Shimura varieties
items.statement: Let (G, X) be a Hodge-type Shimura datum, K = K_pK^p neat, L a p-adic completion of the reflex field and L̆ the completion of its maximal unramified extension. Let S be the basic locus of the rigid generic fibre over L̆ and S̃ the restriction of the infinite-level Shimura variety. Grant the uniformization of the basic locus (deducible from the Igusa-stack fibre product of Daniels–van Hoften–Kim–Zhang). Then S is a disjoint union of quotients (M_{b,[μ]}/K_p)/Γ, with Γ ≤ G_b(Q_p) discrete. Étale locally on S, the diagram S ← S̃ → Fl_[μ] (π_HT) is isomorphic to M_{b,[μ]}/K_p ← M_{b,[μ]} → Fl_[μ], so Theorem A applies étale locally to S̃.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The item copies §10.1, which has two slips (new issue). S is defined over L, a p-adic completion of the reflex field, which is neither strict nor contains Q̆_p. The uniformization by M_{b,[μ]}/K_p, a space over Q̆_p([μ]), holds only after base change to L̆, the completion of the maximal unramified extension of L (§10.2 does base-change to Q̆_p), and Theorem A needs such a field. Also, 'M_{b,[μ]}/K_p × Γ' means the quotient (M_{b,[μ]}/K_p)/Γ. Review note: The uniformization (Rapoport–Zink; Daniels–van Hoften–Kim–Zhang) is planned nowhere in the atlas (searches for 'basic locus', 'Rapoport–Zink uniformi' and 'Igusa stack' find nothing), so status missing is right.

items.name: Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization of Shimura curves
items.statement: For D/Q a quaternion algebra split at ∞ and ramified at p, B the definite quaternion algebra split at p with the other ramification of D, K^p neat and O_p the maximal order of D ⊗ Q_p: B^×(Q)\B^×(A_f) ×_{GL_2(Q_p)} M_{b,[μ]}/O_p^× K^p ≅ S, S the rigid generic fibre of Sh_{O_p^× K^p} over Q̆_p (Boutot–Carayol).
items.note: Review note: HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.5 plans the Boutot–Carayol Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization with the Drinfeld half-plane, formal model and descent datum, so 'planned' is right. The identification with this paper's M_{b,[μ]}/O_p^× is item 171 (route 1).

items.name: Products of Shimura curves as quotients of products of Drinfeld planes
items.statement: M_{b,[μ]}/O_p^× = ⊔_{p^Z} Ω with GL_2(Q_p) permuting the components through v(det), the stabilizer of Ω being GL_2(Q_p)°; S is a finite disjoint union of Ω/Γ indexed by B^×(Q)\p^Z × B^×(A_f^{(p)})/K^p, with Γ ≤ B^×(Q) acting properly discontinuously, so Ω → Ω/Γ is a covering in the analytic topology. For S = ∏ S_i and a component S° = Ω^n/Γ, M_{b,[μ]} is the product of n infinite-level Drinfeld (equivalently Lubin–Tate) spaces.
items.note: Review note: R18.5 plans Ω and the arithmetic quotients Ω/Γ. Identifying M_{b,[μ]}/O_p^× (G = D_p^×, G_b = GL_2) with ⊔_{p^Z} Ω, and the product statement, are not planned. Missing is right.

items.name: Perfectoidness of infinite-level spaces and compatibility of Hodge–Tate period maps
items.statement: The infinite-level Lubin–Tate/Drinfeld spaces are perfectoid (Scholze–Weinstein, Moduli of p-divisible groups), the infinite-level Shimura variety S̃ is perfectoid (Scholze, torsion), and the local and global Hodge–Tate period maps are compatible (Caraiani–Scholze).
items.note: ET.6a constructs the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers; PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S2–S3 the Hodge-type perfectoid tower and its Hodge–Tate period map. Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): Only partly planned. ET.6a plans the Lubin–Tate and Drinfeld towers by Scholze–Weinstein §§6–7, but never states their perfectoidness. PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S2 and S3 plan the Hodge-type perfectoid tower and its Hodge–Tate period map; quaternionic Shimura curves over Q ramified at p are of PEL, hence Hodge, type, so they are covered. No stage plans the Caraiani–Scholze compatibility of the local (Rapoport–Zink) and global Hodge–Tate period maps: searches for 'Caraiani' find only AG2.5 (local–global compatibility), and 'Hodge–Tate period' finds only S3. Review note: Split the item: perfectoidness of the Shimura tower and its π_HT are planned (S2, S3); perfectoidness of the infinite-level Lubin–Tate/Drinfeld spaces should be written into ET.6a; the local–global compatibility of π_HT on the uniformized basic locus is missing (route 1).

items.name: A global bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem for products of Shimura curves
items.statement: For a product S = ∏ S_i of Shimura curves as above (ramified at p), the diagram S° ← S̃|_{S°} = M_{b,[μ]}/Γ' → (P^1)^n is, locally in the analytic topology on S°, isomorphic to M_{b,[μ]}/O_p^× ← M_{b,[μ]} → (P^1)^n, so Theorem A gives a bi-analytic Ax–Lindemann theorem for S̃ (Hodge analytic structure from S, Hodge–Tate from π_HT), disjoint from the bi-algebraic Ax–Lindemann theorem of Chambert-Loir–Loeser for (P^1)^n ⊇ Ω^n → Ω^n/Γ.
items.locator: Section 10.2, pp. 64–66 (diagram p. 65; discussion of the three triangles p. 66); Chambert-Loir–Loeser [10, Theorems 3.4 and 2.7] cited on pp. 62 and 66

items.name: Resolution of singularities of rigid analytic varieties
items.statement: Let k be a non-archimedean field of characteristic zero and S a reduced rigid analytic variety over k. There is a resolution of singularities π: S̃ → S (Temkin, Duke Math. J. 161 (2012), Theorem 5.3.2, as cited by the paper): S̃ is smooth, and π is proper and surjective, a locally finite composite of blow-ups with nowhere-dense centres lying over the singular locus. So π is an isomorphism over the smooth locus S^sm, which is a dense Zariski open, and π^♢ is a v-cover. For an arbitrary rigid variety T (e.g. T = S̃ ×_S S̃) apply this to T_red, which has the same diamond: T^♢ = (T_red)^♢.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.0.4(4), Section 5.3, p. 35 (arXiv v2), citing Temkin, Theorem 5.3.2 (applied to S and to S̃ ×_S S̃); also Section 9.3, p. 60, the sentence before Lemma 9.3.5 ('taking S to be a desingularization of Z'), which proves Lemma 9.3.1 (stated p. 58)
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Three problems. (a) As stated it is false for non-reduced S: a resolution that is an isomorphism over the smooth locus needs S reduced (or at least generically reduced). The fibre product S̃ ×_S S̃ is in general not reduced; the paper resolves it, which is harmless because a rigid space and its reduction have the same diamond. (b) Wrong pages: in Section 5.3 the Temkin citation is on p. 35, not p. 34. (c) The Lemma 9.3.1 quote ('taking S to be a desingularization of Z') is on p. 60, in the sentence before Lemma 9.3.5; Lemma 9.3.1 itself is stated on p. 58. Review note: missing is right. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7 plans resolution only for varieties of finite type over a characteristic-zero field (it explicitly asserts no excellent-scheme resolution), so the rigid-analytic case is not planned. R09.7a (blow-ups) is a usable input for route 3.

items.name: Proper Zariski closed subsets of irreducible rigid spaces are nowhere dense
items.statement: Let X be a connected normal (e.g. smooth connected) rigid analytic variety (Conrad, Irreducible components of rigid spaces, Lemma 2.1.4), or more generally an irreducible one (loc. cit., Lemma 2.2.3). Then a Zariski closed (analytic) subset Z ≠ X contains no non-empty admissible open. Equivalently, dim O_{Z,z} < dim O_{X,z} for all z ∈ Z, and Z is nowhere dense in |X|.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Conrad's Lemma 2.1.4 is stated for connected normal rigid spaces: an analytic subset containing a non-empty admissible open is the whole space. The version for irreducible spaces is Conrad's Lemma 2.2.3. The paper applies Lemma 2.1.4 to S smooth connected, hence normal, which is correct. Review note: Route 3's brief (item 2) repeats the misattribution; correct it there too.

items.name: Weakly Shilov points avoid nowhere dense Zariski closed subsets
items.statement: Let X be a rigid space over a non-archimedean field K. A point x ∈ X is weakly Shilov if it is a Shilov point of some affinoid open neighbourhood (Bhatt–Hansen, Definition 2.5; equivalently, the secondary residue field at x has transcendence degree dim_x X over the residue field of K, Proposition 2.9). Weakly Shilov points are dense in X (Lemma 2.8), and a nowhere dense Zariski closed subset of X contains none of them (Corollary 2.10).
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: Citation numbering: in Bhatt–Hansen (arXiv 2101.09759 v1 and v2), Definition 2.4 defines Shilov points of an affinoid, weakly Shilov points are Definition 2.5, and density is Lemma 2.8. Corollary 2.10 is as cited. Route 3's brief copies 'Definition 2.4'.

items.name: Stratification by smooth subvarieties and the maximal-rank locus
items.statement: Let Y be a reduced rigid analytic variety of finite dimension over a non-archimedean field of characteristic 0. Its singular locus is a nowhere dense Zariski closed subset, so Y = Y_0 ⊇ Y_1 = Sing(Y_0) ⊇ Y_2 = Sing(Y_1) ⊇ … terminates after at most dim Y + 1 steps. Hence Y is a finite disjoint union of smooth Zariski-locally closed subvarieties Y_i − Y_{i+1}. For f: V → W a map of smooth rigid varieties with V connected, the locus where rank df equals its maximum on V is a non-empty Zariski open subset (rank df ≥ r is the non-vanishing of some r × r minor).
items.locator: Section 9.2, p. 56; proof of Theorem 9.1.3, p. 57
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: The '(quasi-compact)' hypothesis does not cover the application. On p. 57, Y is a closed rigid analytic subvariety of M_C/K_b, which is not quasi-compact in general (for Lubin–Tate, the connected components are open polydiscs). What makes the stratification finite is finite dimension. Also, the maximal-rank locus of df is itself Zariski open, not merely a set containing a Zariski open.

items.name: Classical points as p-adic manifolds and the constant rank theorem
items.statement: For V a smooth rigid analytic variety over a p-adic field E and C = Ē^, the classical points V(E') (E'/E finite) and V(C) are analytic manifolds over E' and C in Serre's sense, and a map f: V → W of smooth rigid varieties induces analytic maps with df_C = df|_{T_{V(C)}}. A map of constant rank k is, in suitable charts, (x_1, …, x_m) ↦ (x_1, …, x_k, 0, …, 0) (Serre, Lie algebras and Lie groups, Part II, Chapter III, theorem on subimmersions). The orbit map of G(C) on a homogeneous space is a submersion, and an analytic function vanishing on an open subgroup K_0 ≤ G(Q_p) vanishes near 1 in G(C).
items.locator: Section 9.2, p. 56; proof of Theorem 9.1.3, pp. 57–58
items.note: Review note: Content checked against p. 58. The Serre reference (Lie Algebras and Lie Groups, Part II, Chapter III, theorem on subimmersions) could not be opened here. Mathlib has the inverse and implicit function theorems but no constant rank theorem; route 3's brief (item 6) plans it.

items.name: A closed set containing the points of a disc contains its Gauss point
items.statement: Let L' be a complete discretely valued field with infinite residue field k' (e.g. any finite extension of a p-adic field containing Q̆_p), and D ⊆ S_{L'} a closed n-dimensional L'-polydisc with Gauss point η. Every open neighbourhood of η in |D| contains L'-points. Indeed, a rational neighbourhood {|f_i| ≤ |g|} of η, normalized so that |g|_η = 1, contains every x ∈ O_{L'}^n whose reduction avoids the zero set of ḡ ≠ 0 in k'^n, and such x exist because k' is infinite. Hence a closed subset of |S_{L'}| containing D(L') contains η. Moreover, D(L') ⊆ |S_{L'}| with the subspace topology is homeomorphic to O_{L'}^n.
items.note: Review (REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26): statement corrected against the paper: 'Algebraically closed residue field' is the wrong hypothesis for the application. In Lemma 9.3.5, L' is a finite extension of a p-adic field L ⊇ Q̆_p whose residue field is only perfect (the paper's definition of p-adic field, Section 1.6, p. 12; Remark 1.1.7). The fact holds whenever the residue field is infinite, which holds here since it contains F̄_p. For a finite residue field it fails, e.g. for {x : |x^q − x| ≥ 1} on the unit disc.

items.name: Kottwitz's set B(G, [μ]) for reductive G and its basic element
items.statement: For G/Q_p reductive and [μ] a conjugacy class of cocharacters of G_{Q̄_p}, B(G, [μ]) ⊆ B(G) is the set of [b] with κ_G(b) = μ^# in π_1(G)_Γ and Newton point ν_b ≤ the Galois average of the dominant representative of [μ] (Kottwitz, Isocrystals II, §6); it contains a unique basic class.
items.locator: Section 1.1, p. 3, citing Kottwitz 1997 §6; used in Section 6.2, p. 36, and Section 1.1 footnote 1
items.note: Review note: Missing is right, via source route 6. BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1 plans the Kottwitz map, Newton points, basic classes and the order, but does not name B(G, μ).

items.name: Zariski closedness is transitive for affinoid perfectoid spaces
items.statement: Let Z_2 ⊆ Z_1 ⊆ Z_0 be affinoid perfectoid spaces over a p-adic field L, with Z_1 Zariski closed in Z_0 and Z_2 Zariski closed in Z_1, i.e. Z_2 = V(I) for an ideal I ⊆ O(Z_1). Then Z_2 is Zariski closed in Z_0. Proof: O(Z_0) → O(Z_1) is surjective (Bhatt–Scholze, Prisms, Theorem 7.4 and Remark 7.5). Hence I is generated by images of elements of O(Z_0), and Z_2 = V(J + I') for J the ideal of Z_1 and I' a lift of I.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Lemma 2.3.2 (item 034) uses this, as the remark says; Lemma 2.3.2 in turn gives the closedness of Hodge–Tate loci (Lemma 6.3.2). Item 034's note mentions it, but no item states it. Route: AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures.

items.name: B-local systems on a locally spatial diamond
items.statement: Let X/Spd Q_p be a locally spatial diamond and let B be one of B_dR^+, B_dR, O, viewed as sheaves on X_v. A sheaf of B-modules on X_v is constant if it is isomorphic to B^r. A B-local system on X is a B-module on X_v that is locally constant in the v-topology, and Loc_B(X) is the category of B-local systems. Base change along θ: B_dR^+ → O gives an exact tensor functor Loc_{B_dR^+}(X) → Loc_O(X), and B_dR^+ ⊆ B_dR gives Loc_{B_dR^+}(X) → Loc_{B_dR}(X). Over Spd L, for L a p-adic field, these are L-linear.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): Items 033 and 035 and the whole of Section 3 use Loc_B(X), but only Λ-local systems (item 031) have an item. Route: AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures.

items.name: Commutative unipotent groups are equivariantly vector groups, and the derived-series filtration
items.statement: Let k be a field of characteristic 0, G a linear algebraic group over k and U ⊴ G a normal unipotent subgroup. (1) If U is commutative, the exponential map exp: Lie U → U is an isomorphism of algebraic groups from the vector group of Lie U. It intertwines the adjoint action of G on Lie U with the conjugation action of G on U. (2) Each term of the derived series U = U^{(0)} ⊇ U^{(1)} = [U, U] ⊇ … ⊇ U^{(r)} = 1 is a closed connected subgroup, normal in G. Each quotient U^{(i)}/U^{(i+1)} is commutative unipotent, so by (1) it is G-equivariantly the vector group of Lie U^{(i)}/Lie U^{(i+1)}.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.2.2, p. 28 (arXiv v2); also Remark 4.2.1, p. 27
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): The proof of Theorem 4.2.2 (items 074–075) uses this, and no item covers it. Neither Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups nor the atlas plans exp for unipotent groups or vector-group structures (searched 'vector group|exp … Lie'). Route: ReductiveGroupsStabilizersAndLeviPartII.

items.name: Steinberg's theorem over Q̆_p, and the classification of G-isocrystals by B(G)
items.statement: Let k be a perfect field of cohomological dimension ≤ 1, for example Q̆_p. For every connected linear algebraic group G over k, H^1(k, G) = 0 (Steinberg). Hence, for G a connected linear algebraic group over Q_p, every exact tensor functor Rep G → Vect(Q̆_p) is isomorphic to ω_std ⊗ Q̆_p. So every G-isocrystal is isomorphic to the one attached to some b ∈ G(Q̆_p), and b ↦ (V ↦ (V ⊗ Q̆_p, ρ(b)σ)) induces a bijection from B(G) to the isomorphism classes of G-isocrystals.
items.locator: Section 4.1, p. 26 (arXiv v2); Part I (arXiv:2308.11065v2) Section 2.2.3
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): Item 069 asserts the bijection for non-reductive G. Its proof needs every fibre functor Rep G → Vect(Q̆_p) to be isomorphic to the standard one, and no stage plans that (searched 'Steinberg … H^1 / cohomological dimension'). BG0 plans only the reductive comparison. Route: ReductiveGroupsStabilizersAndLeviPartII.

items.name: The relative Fargues–Fontaine curve FF_S and its cover Y_S
items.statement: For S = Spa(R, R^+) ∈ Perf_{F̄_p} with pseudouniformizer ϖ, Y_S = Spa W(R^+) ∖ V(p[ϖ]) is an analytic adic space over Spa Q̆_p. Glued over affinoid covers, it is defined for all S ∈ Perf_{F̄_p}, and the Frobenius φ acts on it totally discontinuously. FF_S := Y_S/φ^Z is an adic space over Spa Q_p (Fargues–Scholze Definition II.1.15), functorial in S, and Y_S → FF_S is an étale cover. Vector bundles and G-bundles on FF_S are Frobenius-equivariant ones on Y_S.
items.locator: Section 4, p. 25; Section 4.2, p. 27 (arXiv v2), citing Fargues–Scholze Definition II.1.15 and II.1.1
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): Every item of Section 4 is stated on FF_S, but no extraction item defines the curve. It is planned (RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0:integral-Y builds Y_S; RF1 glues Y_S and forms X_S = Y_S/φ^Z), so the item records a planned import for route 1 and asks for no new work.

items.name: Basic strata of Bun_G for reductive G (Fargues–Scholze Theorem III.4.5)
items.statement: Let G/Q_p be a connected reductive group. The semistable locus Bun_G^ss ⊆ Bun_G is open and is the disjoint union of the open and closed substacks Bun_G^b, b ∈ B(G)_basic, of G-bundles that are geometrically isomorphic to E_b. For b basic, Aut(E_b) is the pure inner twist G_b × FF_S (Fargues–Scholze Proposition III.4.2), and E_b induces an isomorphism [∗/G_b(Q_p)] ≅ Bun_G^b.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.2.2, pp. 27–28 (arXiv v2), citing Fargues–Scholze Theorem III.4.5 and Proposition III.4.2
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): The non-reductive theorem (items 074–075) is built on the reductive one, which only item 074's note mentions. Recording it as a planned item makes the dependency on BunGAndNewtonStrata BG3 explicit, like item 180 for BG1.

items.name: Rigid analytic points of the B_dR^+-affine Grassmannian
items.statement: Let G/L be a connected linear algebraic group over a p-adic field L, L′/L a finite extension, and C the completion of an algebraic closure of L′. Every x ∈ Gr_G(Spd L′) lies in Gr_[μ](Spd L′) for a unique conjugacy class [μ] of cocharacters of G_{L̄}, and L([μ]) ⊆ L′. So Gr_G(Spd L′) = ⊔_{[μ]: L([μ]) ⊆ L′} Gr_[μ](Spd L′). For each such [μ], BB is a bijection Gr_[μ](Spd L′) → Fl_[μ^{-1}](L′). Its inverse sends a filtration Fil^• of type [μ^{-1}] on the trivial G-bundle over L′ (always of the form Fil_{μ^{-1}} for a cocharacter μ of G_{L′}) to the Gal(L̄/L′)-invariant lattice L_μ, given for each V ∈ Rep G by L_μ(V) = Σ_i Fil^{-i}V_{L′} ⊗_{L′} Fil^i B_dR(C). Proof: descent plus Proposition 2.3.1 identify Gr_G(Spd L′) with Gal(L̄/L′)-invariant lattices on the trivial G-bundle over B_dR^+(C); then Part I Proposition 3.1.7(2) and Example 3.1.10 (invariant lattices = filtered L′-vector spaces, via the trace filtration).
items.locator: Section 5.3, first paragraph (proof of Theorem 5.0.4(4) for S = Spa L′), pp. 34–35 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): Rigid analytic points of Gr_G all lie in Schubert cells and are exactly the filtered G-bundles over L′. This statement is proved but not numbered, and no item covers it. It is used in Example 5.0.5 (the only rigid point of Gr_{G_a} is 0), in the classical-point step of Lemma 6.3.3, and in the first half of Theorem 5.0.4(4). Item 088 covers only rigid S mapping into Gr_G ×_{Gr_M} Gr_[μ]_M, not all rigid points of Gr_G. Route: AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures.

items.name: Motivic Galois groups of neutral admissible pairs are connected; canonical reductions are neutral over connected bases
items.statement: Let Y/Spd Q̆_p be a locally spatial diamond, G/Q_p a connected linear algebraic group, 𝒢 a neutral G-admissible pair on Y and y a geometric point. (1) MG(𝒢, y) is a connected linear algebraic group. (Proof: an object X ∈ ⟨𝒢⟩ with finite MG(X, y) has, at every geometric point y′, MG(y′^*X) ⊆ MG(X, y′) finite (Deligne–Milne Proposition 2.21(b); MG(X, y′) is an inner form of MG(X, y)), hence trivial since AdmPair(C′) is connected (Part I Theorem 5.1.6); so X is a sum of unit objects (Q̆_p, B_dR^+).) (2) If Y is connected, then for all geometric points y, y′ the fibre functors ω_y and ω_{y′} are isomorphic on ⟨𝒢⟩; hence, after a trivialization ω_y∘𝒢 ≅ ω_std, the canonical reduction of 𝒢 to H = MG(𝒢, y) is a neutral H-admissible pair. (The class of Isom^⊗(ω_y, ω_{y′}) in the finite set H^1(Q_p, H) is locally constant in y′.) (2) fails for disconnected Y.
items.locator: Section 7.2, p. 41 and Section 7.5, p. 46 (arXiv v2); implicit in the paper, supplement of this review from Part I Theorem 5.1.6
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): The paper applies constructions defined only for connected groups (Gr_H, b_H-rigidification by Steinberg's theorem, Theorem 7.2.3) to H = MG(𝒢, y), and calls the canonical reduction a neutral H-admissible pair, without stating either fact; neutrality fails over disconnected bases. Route: AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures.

items.name: The Hodge locus of a line is a disjoint union of twisted admissible loci of its stabilizer
items.statement: Let H ≤ G be connected linear algebraic groups over Q_p with H = Stab_G(ℓ) for a line ℓ in W ∈ Rep G, and b_H ∈ H(Q̆_p) = b_G (so ℓ_Q̆p is a one-dimensional sub-isocrystal of W_{b_G}(W)). Then (1) Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p) ⊆ Gr_G^{b_G-adm} lies in the image of the injection Gr_{H,Q̆_p} → Gr_{G,Q̆_p}; (2) at a geometric point of Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p) the sub-admissible pair on ℓ gives a degree-zero line subbundle of the trivial bundle W ⊗ O, i.e. a Q_p-line [w] ∈ (G/H)(Q_p), and the H-bundle (E_{b_H})_L is the pushforward of the H-torsor G ×_{G/H} [w]; (3) consequently Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p) is the disjoint union, over c ∈ ker(H^1(Q_p, H) → H^1(Q_p, G)) = G(Q_p)\(G/H)(Q_p), of the open loci where (E_{b_H})_L ∈ Bun_H^{[c]} (Theorem 4.2.2), and the piece for c = 1 is the image of Gr_H^{b_H-adm}; in particular Gr_H^{b_H-adm} is open and closed in Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p), hence closed in Gr_G^{b_G-adm}, and equals Hdg(ℓ_Q̆p) when the kernel is trivial. Example with non-trivial kernel: G = SL_2, H the anisotropic norm-one torus of an unramified quadratic extension, b = 1.
items.locator: Proposition 7.5.2, p. 47; proof, pp. 47–48 (arXiv v2), corrected (see the new issue on its proof)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): The key step of the proof (Hdg(ℓ) = Gr_H^{b_H-adm}) is false in general; the corrected lemma is what the proof and later uses of Hodge loci need. Route: AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures.

items.name: The Hodge–Tate analytic Zariski closure of a connected set via connected components
items.statement: Let b be basic, M = M_{b,[μ]}, L/Q̆_p([μ]) a p-adic field, C = L̄^, 𝔍 = Gal(L̄/L), and Z̃ ⊆ M_C connected. Then the Hodge–Tate analytic Zariski closure of Z̃ (Definition 9.1.1) equals ∩ Ỹ. The intersection runs over all compact open K_b ≤ G_b(Q_p) × 𝔍 and all closed rigid analytic subdiamonds Y ⊆ M_C/K_b containing π_{K_b}(Z̃), and Ỹ is the connected component of π_{K_b}^{-1}(Y) containing Z̃. If no such Y exists, the closure is M_C. The same holds with G(Q_p) × 𝔍 for the Hodge closure.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 9.1.3, Eq. (9.2.0.1), pp. 56–57 (arXiv v2)
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): Definition 9.1.1 intersects the full preimages π_{K_b}^{-1}(Y), but the proof works with the connected components Ỹ containing Z̃. That the two intersections agree is a separate topological step: connected components of a limit of finite étale quotients are limits of connected components. A formalization needs it. Route: AdmissiblePairsAndPadicHodgeStructures.

items.name: Products of a locally spatial diamond with a profinite set
items.statement: Let P be a profinite set, viewed as the diamond P̲ = Spd of the locally constant functions, and S a locally spatial diamond. Then |P̲ × S| = P × |S| as topological spaces. The projection P̲ × S → S is proper (quasi-compact, separated and universally closed), so the image in |S| of any closed subset of |P̲ × S| is closed. This applies in particular to P a compact open subset of P_V(Q_p).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-HOWE-KLEVDAL-26 (coverage of the paper): The proof that the Hodge exceptional locus is a countable union of closed sets rests on two facts about products of a locally spatial diamond with a profinite set, and no item records them. Route: DiamondsAndVStacks.
